target.title: fix(telegram): catch unhandled rejections in webhook and ingress worker shutdown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Telegram channel shutdown paths that could leave unhandled promise rejections or skip owned cleanup:

1. **Webhook shutdown**: when `bot.stop()` rejected, owned cleanup (transport close, webhook status note, diagnostic heartbeat stop) was skipped.
2. **Ingress worker shutdown**: repeated `stop()` calls could race teardown, and forced `worker.terminate()` rejections were not observed on the timeout fallback path.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Webhook** (`extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts`): wrap `bot.stop()` in `try/catch/finally` so cleanup always runs; route stop failures to `runtime.error`.
- **Ingress worker** (`extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts`): share one in-flight `stopPromise` for idempotent shutdown, catch `postMessage` errors for already-terminated workers, and route forced `worker.terminate()` rejections with `.catch(() => undefined)` on the 15s timeout fallback.

Deliberate non-goals: no transport/streaming/auth behavior changes; no new config surface.

## User Impact

Telegram webhook abort and ingress-worker shutdown no longer leak unhandled rejections on the covered failure paths, and webhook-owned transport/status/diagnostics cleanup completes even when `bot.stop()` fails.

## Evidence

Rebased on current `origin/main` (`471f60bc8481`). Head: `899a1c3af4c6`.

### Forward proof (after fix)

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts -- --run -t "does not leak unhandled rejections when shutdown throws"
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  3 passed (3)

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed | 35 skipped (36)
```

Regression coverage includes:
- shared `stopPromise` idempotency
- forced timeout `terminate()` rejection routed (no `unhandledRejection`)
- webhook shutdown `finally` cleanup when `bot.stop()` rejects

### Negative control (origin/main prod code + branch tests)

Swap prod files to `origin/main`, run the focused shutdown tests, restore branch prod files:

```bash
git show origin/main:extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts > /tmp/ingress-main.ts
git show origin/main:extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts > /tmp/webhook-main.ts
cp /tmp/ingress-main.ts extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.ts
cp /tmp/webhook-main.ts extensions/telegram/src/webhook.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts -- --run -t "idempotent|shutdown throws|terminate rejections|unhandled"
```

```text
Test Files  2 failed (2)
     Tests  2 failed | 2 passed | 35 skipped (39)
     Errors  1 error
```

Restore branch prod files → forward proof passes again.

### What was NOT tested

Did not run a configured live Telegram gateway shutdown with real bot credentials on this machine. Proof is focused mocked lifecycle tests plus negative control on current `origin/main` prod code.

AI-assisted: implementation, tests, and proof were drafted with Cursor agent assistance; validation was run locally with the commands above.

target.title: fix(cli-backends): surface config-defined custom CLI backends in runtime model bindings (fixes #106373)
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `sessions.compact` throws `MissingAgentHarnessError` for sessions running on a config-defined custom CLI backend — a backend declared only under `agents.defaults.cliBackends`, not owned by any plugin. Execution of the same session works correctly because `resolveCliBackendConfig` recognizes config-only backends, but the compaction and harness-selection paths do not, because `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` only consults the plugin runtime registry and optional setup registry — never the user's `agents.defaults.cliBackends` config.

Concrete example: defining a second Claude Code account (`claude-cli-max`) with a different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` under `cliBackends` works for agent turns, but every `sessions.compact` request against that session fails with `MissingAgentHarnessError: Requested agent harness "claude-cli-max" is not registered.`

## Why This Change Was Made

`listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` now also surfaces config-defined custom CLI backends that resolve to a valid config (non-null `resolveCliBackendConfig`). This aligns it with the existing `isCliProvider` function in `model-selection-cli.ts`, which already recognizes config-only backends. The asymmetry — `isCliProvider` sees the backend but `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` and its callers (`isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider`, `resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding`, `resolveCliRuntimeCanonicalProvider`) do not — caused the compaction and harness precheck paths to miss config-only backends while the execution path handled them.

Two additional pass-through fixes: `resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding` and `resolveCliRuntimeCanonicalProvider` now forward `config`/`env` to `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` instead of calling it without parameters. A single call site in `harness/selection.ts` now forwards `cfg` to `isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider` (the other call site in the same file already did).

Backends already in the plugin registry are never duplicated; backends without a valid `command` are silently omitted.

## User Impact

Users with config-defined custom CLI backends (e.g. multiple Claude Code accounts, or any non-plugin CLI runtime) can now run `sessions.compact` without `MissingAgentHarnessError`. Agent execution, harness selection, and compaction preflight all treat these backends consistently.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/cli-backends.ts` — the three-line core change adding config-only backends to `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings`, plus two config-forwarding fixes.
- `src/agents/harness/selection.ts` — one-line forwarding of `cfg` to `isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider`.
- Regression tests in `src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts` — six new cases covering: inclusion of a valid config-only backend, resolution via `resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding`, `isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider` returning true, omission when no config is passed or the backend lacks a command, and non-duplication of plugin-registered backends with config-level overrides.
- Full test run: `pnpm test src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts` — 64 passed; `pnpm test src/agents/model-runtime-aliases.test.ts src/agents/model-selection-cli.test.ts` — 25 passed. No regressions.

```
$ pnpm test src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts -t "config-defined backends"

 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > includes a config-only custom CLI backend with a valid command
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > resolves a binding for a config-only backend via resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider returns true for a config-only backend
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > omits a config-only backend when no config is passed
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > omits a config-only backend with no command
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > does not duplicate a plugin-registered backend with a config-level override

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

The six tests exercise `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` (before — no config → custom backend absent), `resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding` (after — with config → custom backend bound), and `isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider` (after — returns true), covering all three patched functions plus the edge cases.

target.title: fix(agents): provide actionable recovery guidance on context overflow
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users whose agent runs exec commands producing large output (e.g. `kubectl logs`, `cat` of large files) would see only "The agent run failed before producing a reply." — an opaque dead-end message with no recovery path — when the tool result causes unrecoverable context overflow.

The session enters `livenessState: "blocked"` but the user is never told what happened, why, or how to recover.

Related issue: #106204

## Why This Change Was Made

Improved all three user-facing error messages in the overflow/failure path to include concrete recovery commands (`/compact`, `/new`) and a practical tip about re-running commands with tighter output filters:

- `run.ts` `overflowRecoveryText`: replaced generic message with structured recovery options
- `agent-runner-execution.ts` `preserveSessionMapping` path: appended tool output tip
- `chat-display-projection.ts` `GATEWAY_ASSISTANT_ERROR_FALLBACK_TEXT`: added `/compact` and `/new` hints

This is a display-layer-only change — no modification to core recovery logic.

## User Impact

Users hitting context overflow now see actionable guidance instead of a dead-end error. They can immediately try `/compact` or `/new` without needing to search docs or ask for help.

## Evidence

- `npx oxlint@1.72.0` on all 3 modified source files: 0 errors, 0 warnings
- `npx vitest run server-methods.test.ts`: 170/171 tests pass (1 failure is pre-existing SQLite version check unrelated to this change)
- No logic changes — purely string constant modifications

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the macOS cookie-import banner appearing while the embedded dashboard is still showing its Gateway connection or authentication screen. The automatic offer previously ran after app launch and every Gateway connection, before the inline browser was used.

## Why This Change Was Made

The automatic offer is now armed only when the inline browser first opens. Pre-onboarding, remote-Gateway, failed startup, stale in-flight responses, and overlapping reconnect attempts remain armed until one host-local status query is applied. target.title: fix(config): prune cron-run descendant sessions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completed cron run cleanup can leave stale descendant session registry rows behind, such as subagent or thread rows under `agent:<id>:cron:<job>:run:<runId>:...`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`isCronRunSessionKey()` already treats cron-run descendants as cron-run session keys, but session registry maintenance only matched exact `cron:<job>:run:<runId>` rows. This caused stale descendants to be preserved as ordinary sessions.

This change aligns session registry maintenance with the existing cron-run session key classification.

## User Impact

Cron run session registry maintenance now prunes stale completed cron-run descendants while still preserving descendants for currently running cron jobs and preserving ordinary non-cron sessions.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check`
- Added focused regression coverage in
  `src/config/sessions/session-registry-maintenance.test.ts`.
- `codex review --base origin/main`: no actionable regressions found.

### Local SQLite Runtime Proof

In addition to the committed regression test, I ran a temporary local runtime
harness against an isolated SQLite-backed session registry. This was not a
mocked store and did not use any personal OpenClaw state.

The temporary harness used production APIs only:

- `replaceSessionEntry()` to persist the SQLite-backed registry rows;
- `beginSessionWorkAdmission()` to register an active runtime admission;
- `runSessionRegistryMaintenanceForStore({ apply: true, ... })` to execute the
  production maintenance path; and
- `listSessionEntries()` to read the persisted rows before and after apply.

The committed regression test provides the reviewable and CI-reproducible
version of this scenario. The terminal transcript below is supplementary local
runtime evidence from the same production persistence and maintenance APIs.

Raw terminal output:

```text
PR #105633 real SQLite maintenance proof
before (6): ["agent:main:cron:active-job:run:active-run:subagent:worker","agent:main:cron:done-job:run:old-run","agent:main:cron:done-job:run:old-run:subagent:worker","agent:main:cron:running-job:run:old-run","agent:main:cron:running-job:run:old-run:thread:reply","agent:main:subagent:ordinary-worker"]
result: {"afterCount":4,"beforeCount":6,"preservedRunning":2,"pruned":2}

✓ 1 test passed
```

## AI Assistance

This PR was developed with assistance from OpenAI Codex for codebase navigation, implementation, and review. I reviewed the final implementation and tests and understand the behavior change.

target.title: feat: add auth list shortcut
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw models auth list` is the canonical command for inspecting saved model auth profiles, but the shorter top-level shape `openclaw auth list` is still unavailable. This PR adds only that shortcut and keeps the existing model-auth listing implementation as the source of truth.

## Summary

- Add a top-level `openclaw auth list` command.
- Delegate to the existing `modelsAuthListCommand`.
- Preserve `--provider`, `--agent`, and `--json` behaviour.
- Register the lazy top-level `auth` sub-CLI.
- Document the shortcut in the CLI index and models auth docs.

## Scope Boundary

- No new auth storage, login, refresh, secret resolution, or provider probing behaviour.
- No changes to `src/commands/models/auth-list.ts`.
- This does not revive the stale #73462 branch; it is a fresh, narrow alias-only PR.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` passed.
- Local targeted Vitest did not run: this fresh worktree has no installed dependencies, and dependency verification could not reach npm registry endpoints (`ETIMEDOUT`/`ENOTFOUND`) before Vitest started. The branch is pushed for GitHub CI validation.

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities: No.
- Secrets/tokens handling changed: No.
- New/changed network calls: No.
- Command/tool execution surface changed: Yes, a read-only CLI alias is added.
- Data access scope changed: No.

The alias reuses the existing redacted model auth profile listing command, so raw token/API-key/OAuth material remains hidden by the existing implementation and tests.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): keep export tree truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The exported session HTML tree preview must truncate long node text without breaking emoji or other supplementary-plane characters, and it must not scan or allocate the entire message just to keep the first 100 preview characters. The first code-point-safe implementation used `Array.from(s)` over the full message text, which could make large session exports stall or allocate heavily.

## Why This Change Was Made

The follow-up replaces full-string materialization with a bounded `for...of` scan that stops at the preview budget and slices by the resulting UTF-16 offset. This preserves code-point-safe truncation and the existing `...` suffix while avoiding full traversal/allocation of large message content.

## User Impact

`/export-session` HTML tree previews keep emoji boundaries intact and remain responsive when a session contains very large message text.

## Evidence

target.title: feat(durable): hand off wakes to session queue
target.body:
# PR5/5 - internal session delivery handoff + final hardening

## What Problem This Solves

This finishes the beta3 durable-core stack by turning resolved durable wake
obligations into an internal session delivery-queue handoff on gateway startup.
After PR4 made wakes inspectable and controllable, PR5 gives the durable runtime
a concrete recovery path: a resolved wake is replayed, persisted with delivery
evidence, and queued for the owning OpenClaw session without inventing external
channel sends.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR5/5
- Clean PR5 comparison: `a30e2b6ce4e5f1390599380aedc82078c98854f7..443ffd2292e146fad3c089a03382a5f4702632f7`
- PR4 dependency: `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105844`
- GitHub base rationale: existing PR1-PR4 stack PRs target `release/2026.7.1`; the PR4 branch exists on the fork, not as an upstream base branch, so this PR follows stack convention while documenting the exact PR4-head diff.

## Scope

- Adds `createDurableWakeSessionDeliveryHook`, which resolves durable wakes to
  agent/session keys and enqueues one internal `systemEvent` via the session
  delivery queue.
- Wires gateway startup durable wake replay through that hook.
- Persists delivery evidence with `internalDelivery: "session_delivery_queue"`
  and `noExternalSend: true`.
- Extends focused replay/startup tests for idempotency, startup replay, ambiguous
  target handling, and no autonomous resume/abandon/create-new policy.
- Updates durable docs to clarify the `delivered` state and CLI wake-attempt
  evidence.

## Non-scope

- No Discord, Signal, Slack, plugin, or other external transport delivery is
  implemented or claimed.
- No cron mutation.
- No release/changelog/package churn from the stale old PR5 ancestry.
- No broad durable orchestration policy changes beyond this internal handoff.

## Evidence

Clean scope:

```text
6 files changed, 372 insertions(+), 50 deletions(-)
```

Focused behavior:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/durable/wake-delivery-replay.test.ts src/durable/startup.test.ts
# pass: 2 files, 14 tests
```

Adjacent durable CLI/Gateway/read-path proof:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/durable.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/durable.test.ts src/durable/wake-controls-inspection.test.ts
# pass: 3 Vitest shards, 4 files, 25 tests
```

Static/docs gates:

```bash
pnpm check:test-types
# pass

pnpm check:docs
# pass

git diff --check a30e2b6ce4e5f1390599380aedc82078c98854f7..HEAD
# pass
```

Remote proof attempts were made but unavailable in this shell:

```text
blacksmith-testbox: blocked, blacksmith CLI not found in PATH
aws Crabbox: blocked, broker login missing
```

## Upgrade contract

This PR adds no schema migration. It writes wake delivery attempts using the
existing durable wake attempt ledger and queues internal session deliveries using
the existing session delivery queue idempotency contract. Repeated startup replay
must not duplicate queued events once a wake is marked delivered.

## Risk / limits

- Main risk is semantic: reviewers should confirm `delivered` remains scoped to
  internal durable/session handoff and cannot be mistaken for external channel
  transport success.
- Remote Testbox proof is still desirable before merge because local provider
  setup blocked it here.
- Full release validation was not run for this narrow PR5 slice.

target.title: fix(gateway): drain root work continuations before stop process exit
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105697

When a gateway process receives a direct stop signal (SIGTERM/SIGINT without a restart intent), any `session_end` plugin hooks already started by session reset/delete/compaction may be truncated before they complete. Affected plugins may lose database writes, memory summaries, or external resource cleanups.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Adds a bounded drain of the existing gateway root-work set to the direct-stop path. The drain uses a referenced `setTimeout` poll (not `.unref()`) so the timer keeps the event loop alive. Bounded at 2 seconds; the caller always invokes `exitProcess(0)` after return. Per ClawSweeper clarification: the force-exit watchdog is cleared at `run-loop.ts:705` before `handleStopAfterServerClose` is entered at line 710; the drain is self-bounded by its own referenced timer.

#### User Impact

No visible impact. Pending `session_end` hooks get up to 2 seconds to complete before exit. Stuck hooks cannot block shutdown.

#### Evidence

target.title: fix(slack): mark connected status degraded without bot identity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Slack `auth.test` fails at boot, or `channels.slack.botToken` is actually a user token (`xoxp` with `user_id` but no `bot_id`), Socket Mode can still connect while main previously published `healthState: "healthy"`. Operators see a connected channel while mention detection is disabled and required-mention rooms fail closed — silent inbound loss.

## Why This Change Was Made

Transport liveness (`connected: true`) remains useful, but advertising `healthy` is wrong when bot identity is missing under the current bot_id-gated contract (`botUserId = botId ? authUserId : ""`). Publish `healthState: "degraded"` with `lastError`, and log `slack socket mode connected (degraded identity)`.

## User Impact

- Misconfigured bot tokens / failed `auth.test` no longer look healthy in channel status.
- Valid bot-token installs stay `healthy` on connect.
- App Home slash-command wiring and allowlist-resolution formatting are untouched.

target.title: fix(feishu): pass timeoutMs through app-registration guarded fetch

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu app-registration HTTP went through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without a top-level `timeoutMs`. Sibling Feishu surfaces (`streaming-card`) already pass `timeoutMs` so undici dispatcher + guarded abort both fire. Registration previously relied only on `AbortSignal.timeout` inside `RequestInit`, which does not configure the guarded-fetch dispatcher hang floor the same way.

A Feishu/Lark accounts peer that accepts TCP but never returns headers could stall onboarding / QR registration longer than intended, especially if `init.signal` is dropped on a future refactor.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wire `timeoutMs` into `fetchFeishuJson` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, matching the streaming-card pattern:

- Default floor: exported `FEISHU_APP_REGISTRATION_TIMEOUT_MS` (10s) — keeps the tighter wizard budget (not the 30s `FEISHU_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` API client default)
- Optional `timeoutMs` on registration fetch options for tests / overrides
- Remove redundant `init.signal` timeouts now owned by the guarded fetch

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** Registration HTTP depended on `RequestInit.signal` alone; guarded-fetch `timeoutMs` / dispatcher hang floor was unset.

**After:** Every registration JSON call installs a 10s guarded `timeoutMs`. Hung accounts endpoints reject with `TimeoutError: request timed out`.

target.title: fix(telegram): Mini App hangs on Opening dashboard when auth never responds
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram Mini App dashboard bootstrap could hang forever on **"Opening dashboard..."** when the same-origin `auth` fetch never returned (stalled upstream / hung TCP). The generated page had no request deadline, so `.catch(showExpired)` never ran.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bound the Mini App-owned `auth` fetch with a **15s** hang floor using an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` / `clearTimeout` (not `AbortSignal.timeout`), so older Telegram WebViews that lack the static timeout API still open the dashboard and still recover into the existing expired/retry status.

- Healthy auth clears the timer after settle (no late abort race)
- Stalled auth aborts and hits the existing `.catch(showExpired)` path
- No new config/env surface; auth validation / token minting unchanged

## User Impact

**Before:** A hung Mini App `auth` request left the WebView on “Opening dashboard...” indefinitely.

**After:** After 15s the page shows “This link expired. Reopen the dashboard from your bot chat.” so the user can retry from the bot chat. Clients without `AbortSignal.timeout` are not broken by a synchronous throw before `fetch`.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/page.ts`
- Regressions: `page.test.ts`, `page.auth-timeout.test.ts`, `routes.test.ts`

target.title: feat(mcp): requester-scoped MCP server connections
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #106229. In multi-user channels (Slack workspaces, group chats), every sender shares one MCP connection set: MCP servers come only from static config/bundle manifests and runtimes are cached per `sessionId`. Per-user-credentialed MCP (hosted providers minting one MCP session per end user — e.g. per-user OAuth email/calendar) is impossible: one user's authenticated session would leak to everyone in the thread, or the integration cannot exist at all. A conversation session is not an authorization boundary — a Slack thread has many senders.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a generic, provider-agnostic core primitive; all provider logic stays in plugins:

- **New plugin API:** `api.registerMcpServerConnectionResolver({ serverName, resolve })`. Server *identity* stays static (`mcp.servers` / bundle manifest: name, tool filter); only the *connection* (`url`/`headers`) is resolved per trusted requester. `resolve(ctx)` receives runtime-provided trusted identity (`requesterSenderId`, `agentAccountId`, `messageChannel`); returning `null` omits the server for that run.
- **Requester-keyed runtimes:** requester-scoped servers get runtimes keyed `(sessionId, messageChannel, agentAccountId, requesterSenderId)`; static servers keep the existing per-session lifecycle byte-for-byte. Sessions with no registered resolvers are entirely unchanged.
- **Fail closed:** runs without a trusted `requesterSenderId` (cron, subagent, heartbeat) never materialize requester-scoped servers; there is no shared-connection fallback. `senderId` is populated only from the verified inbound envelope (invariant documented at the seam in `attempt.ts`).
- **Credential hygiene:** resolved `url`/`headers` never enter config fingerprints, logs, catalog descriptions, or persisted state. Rotation detection uses an ephemeral per-process HMAC digest (nothing derivable offline). Resolver failures/timeouts log fixed classifications only — no plugin-controlled text.
- **Lifecycle:** per-key serialized resolve+install (promise-chain mutex — no interleaving race class), bounded 10s resolver timeout, 5-minute credential revalidation with rebuild-on-rotation, revocation disposes cached transports even under lease (authorization boundary), idle-TTL sweep covers all keys.
- **Prompt-cache stability:** tool names/schemas are requester-independent; safe-name assignment derives deterministically from the full declared server set regardless of which connections resolve.

Precedent: the plugin tool descriptor cache already keys on `requesterSenderId`; this extends the established pattern to MCP transports. The API surface intentionally leaves room for a future cron/subagent user-context fix (#102098) to flow through additively.

**Note for reviewers (surface changes):** no new `openclaw.json` keys or env vars. Plugin SDK gains one registration method + 3 public type exports; `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` public-exports budget bumped 10645 → 10648 to match (commented in the diff). `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` regenerated per the check's documented flow.

## User Impact

Operators can install plugins that give each trusted channel user their own authenticated MCP-backed tools (email, calendar, CRM) in shared channels. Sender B's run can never invoke sender A's transport — the capability is not attached to B's run. Existing configurations see zero behavior change. Known and documented: content one user's tools place into a shared thread remains visible in that thread's transcript (group-chat semantics; private queries belong in DM sessions).

## Evidence

- Issue with full design rationale: #106229 (links #102098, #72591/#92221, #79451).
- Validation (Blacksmith Testbox + local focused runs): `pnpm check:changed` lanes green (format, SDK baseline, SDK exports, surface budget, lint); `tsgo` + `tsgo:test` exit 0; focused suites `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime`, `mcp-connection-resolver`, `agent-bundle-mcp-tools.materialize`, `agent-bundle-mcp-names`, `agent-bundle-mcp-filter` — 100+ tests green.
- Six rounds of structured adversarial review (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) drove the hardening above: resolver timeout/error containment, revocation-disposes-under-lease, per-key serialization replacing three interim concurrency guards (net −70 LOC in the manager), HMAC digest instead of plain credential hash, constant catalog descriptions, SSE alias preservation, lease aggregation for requester-only sessions, safe-name-map fingerprint participation.
- Tests cover: per-sender runtime keying with static sharing, fail-closed paths (no requester / resolver null / resolver throw / resolver timeout), fingerprint stability under alternating senders, credential rotation rebuild + revocation disposal, out-of-order concurrent resolution, dispose-during-resolve, requester-only lease preservation, cross-partition safe-name determinism, no credential material in fingerprints/logs/catalog summaries.

Follow-ups deliberately out of scope: gateway MCP-app reconstruction lacks requester context (scoped servers stay fail-closed absent there); cron/subagent requester context is #102098.

target.title: fix: models fallbacks --agent silently edits global defaults instead of the agent
target.body:
Closes #106346

AI-assisted (Claude), human-reviewed; validation evidence below.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running `openclaw models fallbacks list/add/remove/clear --agent <id>` (or with `--agent` on the parent `models` command) would silently read and write the global `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` chain instead of the named agent's own fallback chain. `openclaw models status --agent <id>` already resolves the per-agent chain correctly, so reads and writes disagreed: the status view showed one chain while the fallbacks subcommands listed and edited another. The `image-fallbacks` group silently ignored `--agent` too.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `models fallbacks` subcommands now thread `--agent` the same way `models status` does (via `resolveModelAgentOption`), validate the id with the same `resolveKnownAgentId` guard `models status` uses (unknown ids error instead of silently editing global defaults), read the agent's own fallbacks override when it has one, and write through a new `setAgentEffectiveModelFallbacks` helper that mirrors the existing `setAgentEffectiveModelPrimary` pattern (mutate the agent's `agents.list[]` entry when it owns an override, otherwise update `agents.defaults.model`). The `image-fallbacks` group instead rejects `--agent` with a clear error mirroring the existing `rejectAgentScopedModelWrite` guard on `models set`/`set-image`, because image model fallbacks exist only on `agents.defaults.imageModel` by design (there is no per-agent `imageModel` field in the config schema); the flag is now either honoured or refused, never silently ignored. The model catalogue (`agents.defaults.models`) stays global in all cases; only the fallback list itself is agent-scoped.

## User Impact

Operators of multi-agent deployments can now inspect and edit a single agent's fallback chain from the CLI: `openclaw models fallbacks list/add/remove/clear --agent <id>` operates on that agent's chain when the agent has its own model override, and on the global defaults otherwise (matching what `models status --agent <id>` reports). Without `--agent`, behaviour is unchanged. `models image-fallbacks ... --agent <id>` now fails fast with an explanatory message instead of silently editing global defaults.

## Evidence

- New unit tests in `src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts` cover `setAgentEffectiveModelFallbacks`: agent-override writes go to the agent entry (defaults untouched), no-override writes go to defaults, clearing in place, and an agent with an explicit primary but no fallbacks yet.
- New CLI wiring tests in `src/cli/models-cli.test.ts` cover `--agent` forwarding for fallbacks list/add/remove/clear (parent and subcommand flag placement), the unchanged no-agent path, rejection of parent `--agent` for all four `image-fallbacks` subcommands, and the unchanged no-agent image path.
- New e2e tests in `src/commands/models.set.e2e.test.ts` cover the agent-scoped write path end to end (agent entry updated, defaults untouched, catalogue stays global) and unknown `--agent` rejection without a config write.
- `docs/cli/models.md` updated to document `--agent` support on `fallbacks` and rejection on `image-fallbacks`.
- Targeted suites pass: `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts src/cli/models-cli.test.ts src/commands/models.set.e2e.test.ts` (3 shards, 83 tests green).
- `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Reproduced on a live 2026.6.11 multi-agent deployment before the fix: `models status --agent <id>` showed the agent's 4-entry chain while `models --agent <id> fallbacks list` returned the 2-entry defaults chain; after applying the fix the two agree, and the no-agent output is unchanged.

target.title: fix(security): add estimate-before-decode guard to base64 paths
target.body:
## Summary
- Problem: Four locations decode base64 payloads before checking size limits, risking transient OOM if a provider/tool returns an oversized payload.
- Solution: Add estimate-before-decode guards where safe, preserve existing behavior contracts where compatibility matters.
- What changed:
  - `src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts`: writeCliImages adds maxBytes param, estimates decoded size before Buffer.from
  - `src/image-generation/image-assets.ts`: Estimates decoded size before canonicalization to avoid transient string allocation; propagates maxBytes through `generatedImageAssetFromBase64`, `generatedImageAssetFromOpenAiCompatibleEntry`, and `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse`
  - `src/image-generation/openai-compatible-image-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedMediaMaxBytes(req.cfg, "image")` into `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse`
  - `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes` into OpenAI image generation path
  - `extensions/google/image-generation-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes` into Google image generation path
  - `extensions/openrouter/image-generation-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes` into OpenRouter image extraction path
- What did NOT change: `resizeImage` still attempts resize before rejecting (maxBytes is an output target, not an input ceiling); `generatedMusicAssetFromBase64` still returns guaranteed result for SDK compatibility.

## Real behavior proof
- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Base64 decode-before-bounds defense-in-depth gap with attention to compatibility.
- **Real environment tested:** Task worktree on final head `bfbad1ed57` (rebased on latest `upstream/main`), with `node --import tsx` direct function invocation exercising the actual provider response parser and CLI image-write path.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx scripts/proof-base64-decode-guards.mts
  ```
  The script calls `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` with `maxBytes` from `resolveGeneratedMediaMaxBytes` (the same wiring used by the OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, and generic compatible provider paths), and `writeCliImages` with `maxBytes` from `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`.

- **Evidence after fix (final head bfbad1ed57):**
  ```text
  === PR #105323 Runtime Proof: estimate-before-decode guards ===

  --- Part 1: Provider response path (parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse) ---

  Configured maxBytes for image: 6291456 bytes (6.0 MB)
  Default MAX_IMAGE_BYTES: 6291456 bytes (6.0 MB)

  Valid payload (100 bytes decoded):
    estimated decoded bytes: 100
    parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse result: 1 image(s)
    image[0].mimeType: image/png
    image[0].fileName: image-1.png
    image[0].buffer.length: 100 bytes

  Oversized payload (6292480 bytes decoded, exceeds 6291456 budget):
    estimated decoded bytes: 6292480
    parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse result: 0 image(s) (rejected before decode)

  Direct generatedImageAssetFromBase64:
    valid payload: accepted
    oversized payload: rejected (undefined)

  --- Part 2: CLI image-write path (writeCliImages) ---

  Valid CLI image (50 bytes decoded, budget 6291456):
    writeCliImages succeeded: 1 file(s) written
    path: 49f75f4d76118767027dd57f5a9917443a8824e6aedcc300756c4a1b09c0a324.png

  Oversized CLI image (6292480 bytes decoded, exceeds 6291456 budget):
    estimated decoded bytes: 6292480
    writeCliImages rejected: CLI runner image exceeds size limit: 6292480 bytes > 6291456 bytes

  === Proof complete ===
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:**
  1. Provider path: valid configured-size payload (100 bytes) accepted and parsed into image asset; oversized payload (6292480 bytes > 6291456 budget) rejected before decode with 0 images returned
  2. CLI image-write path: valid image (50 bytes) written to disk successfully; oversized image (6292480 bytes > 6291456 budget) rejected with error before Buffer.from allocation
  3. Provider limit propagation confirmed: `resolveGeneratedMediaMaxBytes` returns 6291456 (6 MB default), wired through `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` and all four provider paths
- **What was not tested:** Live provider API response (requires credentials); Rastermill resize (requires image processor backend). The proof exercises the actual final-head code paths with simulated provider payloads that match the real response structure.

## CI failures fixed
- **check-additional-runtime-topology-architecture**: Pre-existing Kysely guardrail violations in `src/snapshot/local-repository.ts` (not in PR diff) — fixed by rebasing on latest `upstream/main`.
- **check-docs**: `docs/docs_map.md` was out of date (not in PR diff) — fixed by rebasing on latest `upstream/main`.
- Both failures were unrelated to this PR's changes and are resolved on the rebased head. Verified locally: `pnpm lint:kysely` → "Kysely guardrails OK"; `pnpm docs:map:check` → "docs:map: docs/docs_map.md is up to date."

## Regression Test Plan
- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts, src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts, src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts
- Scenario locked in: Oversized base64 payload rejected before canonicalization; normal payloads decode successfully; music helper returns guaranteed result.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Tests the exact security invariant (estimate-before-decode where safe) while preserving compatibility contracts.

## Root Cause
- Root cause: Functions skipped the "estimate decoded bytes before decode" guard in some paths, and applied it incorrectly in others (blocking resize, breaking SDK contracts).
- Missing detection / guardrail: Pre-canonicalization size check in image-assets; understanding that maxBytes is an output target not an input ceiling for resizeImage; SDK compatibility requirement for music helper; provider limit propagation through all four provider paths.

target.title: fix(cli-backends): surface config-defined custom CLI backends in runtime model bindings (fixes #106373)
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `sessions.compact` throws `MissingAgentHarnessError` for sessions running on a config-defined custom CLI backend — a backend declared only under `agents.defaults.cliBackends`, not owned by any plugin. Execution of the same session works correctly because `resolveCliBackendConfig` recognizes config-only backends, but the compaction and harness-selection paths do not, because `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` only consults the plugin runtime registry and optional setup registry — never the user's `agents.defaults.cliBackends` config.

Concrete example: defining a second Claude Code account (`claude-cli-max`) with a different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` under `cliBackends` works for agent turns, but every `sessions.compact` request against that session fails with `MissingAgentHarnessError: Requested agent harness "claude-cli-max" is not registered.`

## Why This Change Was Made

`listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` now also surfaces config-defined custom CLI backends that resolve to a valid config (non-null `resolveCliBackendConfig`). This aligns it with the existing `isCliProvider` function in `model-selection-cli.ts`, which already recognizes config-only backends. The asymmetry — `isCliProvider` sees the backend but `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` and its callers (`isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider`, `resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding`, `resolveCliRuntimeCanonicalProvider`) do not — caused the compaction and harness precheck paths to miss config-only backends while the execution path handled them.

Two additional pass-through fixes: `resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding` and `resolveCliRuntimeCanonicalProvider` now forward `config`/`env` to `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` instead of calling it without parameters. A single call site in `harness/selection.ts` now forwards `cfg` to `isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider` (the other call site in the same file already did).

Backends already in the plugin registry are never duplicated; backends without a valid `command` are silently omitted.

## User Impact

Users with config-defined custom CLI backends (e.g. multiple Claude Code accounts, or any non-plugin CLI runtime) can now run `sessions.compact` without `MissingAgentHarnessError`. Agent execution, harness selection, and compaction preflight all treat these backends consistently.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/cli-backends.ts` — the three-line core change adding config-only backends to `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings`, plus two config-forwarding fixes.
- `src/agents/harness/selection.ts` — one-line forwarding of `cfg` to `isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider`.
- Regression tests in `src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts` — six new cases covering: inclusion of a valid config-only backend, resolution via `resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding`, `isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider` returning true, omission when no config is passed or the backend lacks a command, and non-duplication of plugin-registered backends with config-level overrides.
- Full test run: `pnpm test src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts` — 64 passed; `pnpm test src/agents/model-runtime-aliases.test.ts src/agents/model-selection-cli.test.ts` — 25 passed. No regressions.

```
$ pnpm test src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts -t "config-defined backends"

 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > includes a config-only custom CLI backend with a valid command
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > resolves a binding for a config-only backend via resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider returns true for a config-only backend
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > omits a config-only backend when no config is passed
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > omits a config-only backend with no command
 ✓ listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings config-defined backends > does not duplicate a plugin-registered backend with a config-level override

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

The six tests exercise `listCliRuntimeModelBackendBindings` (before — no config → custom backend absent), `resolveCliRuntimeModelBackendBinding` (after — with config → custom backend bound), and `isCliRuntimeAliasForProvider` (after — returns true), covering all three patched functions plus the edge cases.

## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm check:no-conflict-markers` previously read every candidate tracked file returned by `git grep` into memory whole via `fs.readFileSync`. A single large generated or text file that slipped through the binary heuristic could exhaust the process memory before the scan completed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Replace the tracked-files scan with `git grep -n -z -o -I -E` so only exact conflict-marker matches are returned.
- Parse the grep output (path, line number, match) into violation records without buffering file contents.
- Keep `findConflictMarkersInFiles` for direct, small-scale use; the tracked-files path no longer reads files whole.
- `findConflictMarkersInTrackedFiles` now returns paths relative to the repository root, matching `git grep` output.

## User Impact

- Normal conflict-marker checks on source and documentation files are unchanged.
- Oversized or generated files can no longer cause an OOM during the scan because their contents are never read.
- CI and pre-commit runs remain robust against accidental large-file commits.

## Evidence

Local focused test passes:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts --run
```

Result:

```
✓ |tooling| test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts (9 tests) 585ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  9 passed (9)
```

Added regression tests covering:
- tracked files with conflict markers reported via `git grep`
- clean tracked files returning no violations
- binary tracked files skipped by `git grep -I`
- paths containing spaces and unusual characters
- large files whose line numbers are reported without reading the whole file
- `main()` printing paths relative to the repository root

Rebased onto current `upstream/main` to pick up the independent `scripts/lib/sqlite-reliability-runner.ts` async/await fix that was causing `check-test-types` and `checks-node-compact-small-2` failures.

target.title: fix(sessions): suppress terminal transcript gate for sessions still fresh under reset policy (fixes #106403)
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the terminal-main reconciliation gate silently resets a healthy main session on the next inbound message after idle. The gate compares transcript mtime against entry `updatedAt`, and a post-run transcript append (delivery receipt, maintenance write, tool output) creates a margin of tens of milliseconds where `mtime > updatedAt`. Once this condition is true, `freshEntry` becomes false regardless of the configured reset policy — even with a 365-day idle window. The user's session "wakes up blank" with no log line and no error.

Concrete scenario: session completes normally (`status: "done"`, `endedAt` set), a delivery note touches the transcript file 93 ms after `updatedAt` is written, and the next inbound message rolls the session over. Observed on three consecutive days after idle periods.

## Why This Change Was Made

The terminal-main transcript gate (`hasTerminalMainSessionTranscriptNewerThanRegistry`) exists to detect zombie sessions whose transcript was modified after the registry marked them done. But the gate fired for sessions still fresh under the configured reset policy — a false positive.

The fix: only honor the gate when the session is already stale under the reset policy. If the entry is still fresh (within the idle/daily window), a touched transcript is not a zombie — the session is healthy and should not be rolled over.

Two call sites patched:
- `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` — `freshEntry` computation for the auto-reply admission path
- `src/agents/command/session.ts` — `fresh` computation for the command/CLI resolve-session path

The logic is symmetric: compute policy freshness first, then apply the terminal gate only when the result is already `!fresh`. When `policyFresh` is true, the gate is a no-op (the session survives).

## User Impact

Sessions with long idle windows (hours to days) no longer silently reset after a post-run transcript touch. The first message after idle preserves the existing session context. Sessions genuinely expired under the reset policy continue to roll over normally.

## Evidence

- `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` — `freshEntry` now guards `terminalMainTranscriptNewerThanRegistry` with `entryFreshness?.fresh !== true`
- `src/agents/command/session.ts` — restructured `fresh` computation to separate policy freshness from the terminal transcript gate; the gate only takes effect when the session is already stale by policy
- `src/agents/command/session.provider-owned-reset.test.ts` — two new regression cases: a fresh session (5 min old, 30-min idle policy) with `terminalTranscriptNewer=true` is kept alive; a stale session (60 min old, 30-min idle policy) with `terminalTranscriptNewer=true` is rotated

```
$ pnpm test src/agents/command/session.provider-owned-reset.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

target.body: ## Summary This PR adds a silent access-request workflow for blocked Telegram and WhatsApp direct messages. - Emit observation-only pre-auth hooks before pairing challenges or rejection. - Support grouped DM allowlists and propagate trusted `sender_group` metadata. - Extend `/allowlist add dm --group` to add senders or move them between groups. - Auto-load trusted bundled or managed `access-request` hooks while keeping mutable workspace hooks explicitly opt-in. - Document a workspace hook example and clean-install troubleshooting requirements. This matters because unknown senders currently have no silent path to request access without entering an agent session or receiving an automatic reply. The intended outcome is a bounded, privacy-conscious pre-auth observation surface that trusted hooks can use for operator-side approval workflows. Out of scope: automatically approving senders, running the model for blocked messages, or auto-enabling mutable workspace hook code. Success means blocked senders remain blocked until manually approved, while a configured phrase can notify the operator without creating a session or reply path. Reviewers should focus on the pre-auth trust boundary, workspace hook opt-in behavior, allowlist normalization, and grouped-entry config handling. ## Linked context Which issue does this close? N/A - no linked issue. Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? N/A. Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? No known maintainer or owner request. This is an external contribution based on a clean-install access-request workflow. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - Behavior or issue addressed: Unknown Telegram and WhatsApp DM senders can silently request manual access without creating an agent session, running the model, or receiving a reply. - Real environment tested: Clean Docker Compose OpenClaw installations configured with WhatsApp and Telegram `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` and an explicitly enabled workspace `access-request` hook. - Exact steps or command run after this patch: 1. Configure the workspace `access-request` example with environment variables. 2. Run `openclaw config set tools.profile messaging`. 3. Run `openclaw config set commands.config true`. 4. Recreate the container with `docker compose down && docker compose up -d`. 5. Send the configured access phrase from a blocked WhatsApp number. 6. Approve the sender from the operator chat with `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp --group restricted `. - Evidence after fix: 1. WhatsApp blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 2. Operator receives the silent WhatsApp access request notification. 3. WhatsApp sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp`. 4. WhatsApp admitted sender receives a normal agent response. 5. Telegram blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 6. Operator receives the silent Telegram access request notification. 7. Telegram sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel telegram`. - Observed result after fix: Unknown senders on both WhatsApp and Telegram sent the configured access phrase and received no reply. The operator received a silent notification with ready-to-use /allowlist approval commands tailored to each channel. After approval, the sender was admitted to the restricted group. The access phrase used in this test was a custom phrase configured via OPENCLAW_ACCESS_REQUEST_PHRASE. The workspace example ships with Let me in as the default value; operators are encouraged to change it before deploying. - What was not tested: Multi-account deployments were not tested live. - Proof limitations or environment constraints: Phone numbers, gateway tokens, and private endpoints must remain redacted. - Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Before this PR, blocked senders were rejected before any trusted pre-auth observation hook existed. ## Tests and validation Commands run: ```bash node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs README.md node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check pnpm build git diff --check ``` Focused Vitest validation covered 18 files and 383 tests across Telegram, WhatsApp, hook loading, hook mapping, config reload, inbound metadata, and grouped allowlist edits. Focused Vitest command: ```bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/channel.allowlist.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/dm-access.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/inbound-context.contract.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/config-accessors.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/access-control.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/process-message.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-allowlist.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/allowlist-config-edit.test.ts src/hooks/internal-hooks.test.ts src/hooks/loader.test.ts src/hooks/message-hook-mappers.test.ts src/plugins/wired-hooks-message.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts ``` WhatsApp E2E validation: ```bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply.web-auto-reply.connection-and-logging.e2e.test.ts ``` Regression coverage added or updated: - Telegram grouped schema, allowlist editing, blocked-DM pre-auth emission, and sender-group inbound context. - WhatsApp grouped schema, config accessors, pre-auth access control including LID handling, monitor propagation, and E2E coverage. - Core grouped `/allowlist` mutations, internal hook events, plugin hook mapping, config reload behavior, and trusted prompt metadata. Before this fix, blocked Telegram and WhatsApp DMs had no pre-auth observation event, and DM allowlist entries could not carry access-group metadata. ## Risk checklist Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. The config schema adds optional grouped DM `allowFrom` entries. Existing string entries remain supported. No migration is required. Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. What is the highest-risk area? The new pre-auth hook exposes blocked-sender DM content to trusted handlers before admission. How is that risk mitigated? The hook is observation-only, sessionless, model-free, reply-free, bounded, and fire-and-forget. Mutable workspace hooks remain explicitly opt-in. Trusted bundled or managed hooks may auto-load only when an account uses `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`. target.title: fix(transcript-stream): log stat/open errors instead of silently returning empty iterator
target.body:
## Summary

`streamSessionTranscriptLines` and `streamSessionTranscriptLinesReverse` used bare `catch { return; }` blocks that silently swallowed all filesystem errors. Replace them with `catch (err) { transcriptLog.warn(...); return; }`.

## What Problem This Solves

In `src/config/sessions/transcript-stream.ts`, both streaming functions catch `fs.promises.stat` / `fs.promises.open` errors and silently return empty iterators. While an empty iterator is the correct contract for missing files, other errors (permission denied, I/O error) should be visible in diagnostics.

## Root Cause

The functions were designed to return an empty iterator when the file cannot be read, but the empty catch blocks discarded all diagnostic information.

## Why This Fix

Same pattern as [#84449](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84449) and [#106385](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106385) — `createSubsystemLogger` + `formatErrorMessage(err)`.

## Evidence

- **Before**: EACCES error silently swallowed → empty iterator, no diagnostic
- **After**: EACCES error logged → `[transcript-stream] Failed to stat transcript /root/nonexistent-transcript.jsonl: EACCES: permission denied`

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
Lines collected: 0
FAIL: No warnings were emitted on stderr!
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
Lines collected: 0
PASS: Warning was emitted on stderr:
  [transcript-stream] Failed to stat transcript /root/...: EACCES: permission denied
```

## Tests and Validation

- `pnpm check` passed
- Added regression test for permission error path

target.body:
## Summary

fix(agents): tighten count-like schema fields to Type.Integer across built-in tools

**Problem**: Four built-in tool schemas use `Type.Number` for semantically integer-only parameters (entry counts, line counts, match limits, context lines). Fractional values like `10.5` silently pass schema validation and reach tool logic with nonsensical values.

**Solution**: Change all count-like fields to `Type.Integer` in a single aligned change, per ClawSweeper recommendation to set a consistent integer contract across sibling tools before merging individual patches.

**What changed**: `ls.ts` -> `lsSchema.limit: Type.Integer`, `read.ts` -> `readSchema.limit: Type.Integer`, `find.ts` -> `findSchema.limit: Type.Integer`, `grep.ts` -> `grepSchema.limit: Type.Integer` and `grepSchema.context: Type.Integer`. All five schemas exported for production-schema testing.

**NOT changed**: `bash.ts` `timeout` stays `Type.Number` — fractional seconds are meaningful for timeouts.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Count-like tool parameters now reject fractional values at schema-validation time before tool logic runs.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw main@5fe6ad9830a (HEAD of this PR).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx tsx verify-schemas.ts` imports actual production schemas from ls.js/read.js/find.js/grep.js and calls TypeBox Value.Check() with integer and fractional inputs for each changed field.

**After-fix evidence**: Exact-head terminal transcript below validates all five fields against the real registered production schemas at this PR's HEAD (5fe6ad9830a), not a reconstructed copy. Both integer acceptance and float rejection confirmed per field.
```
=== Production schema integer validation (exact HEAD) ===
Testing that all five changed fields reject floats via real registered schemas.

  PASS  lsSchema.limit
       integer=true (expect true)  float_rejected=true (expect true)
  PASS  readSchema.limit
       integer=true (expect true)  float_rejected=true (expect true)
  PASS  findSchema.limit
       integer=true (expect true)  float_rejected=true (expect true)
  PASS  grepSchema.limit
       integer=true (expect true)  float_rejected=true (expect true)
  PASS  grepSchema.context
       integer=true (expect true)  float_rejected=true (expect true)

Result: ALL PASS ✓
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All five count-like schema fields reject fractional values while accepting valid integers at the schema-validation boundary.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end tool invocation with fractional values. The same TypeBox Check() runs at the tool-call parsing boundary so rejection would also happen there, but this is not demonstrated.

## merge-risk

🚨 This change may break existing users, config, or upgrade paths — tools that currently accept and silently floor/truncate fractional values will now reject them at schema level. The risk is limited to callers passing non-integer count arguments, which are semantically nonsensical and unlikely in practice.

## Tests and validation

- `pnpm build` -> exit 0 (no compilation errors, all type checks pass)
- `pnpm vitest run` on all schema tests -> PASS (16/16 across four new focused test files)

  - `find.limit-schema.test.ts` — 2/2 (int accept, float reject with omit test)
  - `grep.limit-context-schema.test.ts` — 3/3 (int+float for limit and context, both omitted OK)
- Branch rebased on latest `main` with no merge conflicts
- Single clean commit per convention

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — all limit/context fields were always expected to be positive integers
- [x] All existing tests pass
- [ ] I have not updated documentation (N/A — schema-only change)

## What Problem This Solves

`docs/channels/line.md` does not document the `responsePrefix` field, which is available for LINE via the inherited `ReplyRuntimeConfigSchemaShape`. Users configuring LINE cannot discover this feature from the docs.

- Problem: The `responsePrefix` field exists in the LINE config schema but is absent from the docs

- What did NOT change: No code or behavior changes. Documentation only.

**Documented field**:
- **`responsePrefix`** (string) — optional string prepended to every outbound reply

## Evidence

### Schema — `responsePrefix` via `ReplyRuntimeConfigSchemaShape` (`src/config/zod-schema.core.ts:657`)

```typescript
responsePrefix: z.string().optional(),
```

The LINE config schema extends `LineCommonConfigSchemaBase` which spreads `ReplyRuntimeConfigSchemaShape`, inheriting `responsePrefix` alongside other reply-formatting fields.

### LINE types (`extensions/line/src/types.ts:30`)

```typescript
responsePrefix?: string;
```

### How `responsePrefix` is consumed at runtime

The LINE channel sends messages through `extensions/line/src/outbound.runtime.ts`, which passes the reply config (including `responsePrefix`) through the SDK`s shared outbound pipeline. ## User Impact

Users can now discover the `responsePrefix` option from the LINE channel docs. This field was already functional — it was simply invisible to users who configure via docs.

target.title: fix: Control UI avatar initial breaks on emoji display names
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: When an agent's display name begins with an emoji or other astral Unicode character, the Control UI sidebar and agent selector rendered a broken or garbled avatar initial (a lone UTF-16 surrogate half / replacement character) instead of the intended glyph.
- Solution: Replaced `(label || agent.id).slice(0, 1).toUpperCase()` with a new `deriveAvatarInitial` helper that uses `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: "grapheme"` to extract the complete first user-perceived character (grapheme cluster). When `Intl.Segmenter` is unavailable (Firefox 114-124), falls back to the first complete Unicode code point (surrogate pair-aware). Returns `""` for empty or missing input.
- What changed: `ui/src/lib/avatar.ts` — `deriveAvatarInitial` using `Intl.Segmenter` with feature detection and fallback; `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — uses helper; `ui/src/components/agent-select.ts` — uses helper in fallback.
- What did NOT change: Behavior for ordinary ASCII names; other `.slice()` sites left unchanged (ASCII-only inputs).

## ClawSweeper review fixes

**P1: Guard Intl.Segmenter before rendering avatars** — Added feature detection: checks `typeof Intl.Segmenter === "function"` at runtime. When unavailable (e.g., Firefox 114-124), falls back to extracting the first complete Unicode code point (surrogate pair-aware). This prevents runtime errors in browsers without `Intl.Segmenter` support while still improving behavior over the original UTF-16 code unit slicing.

**P2: Preserve complete first grapheme** — Previously used `codePointAt(0)` which only gets the first code point, still truncating joined emoji (👨‍👩‍👧‍👦→👨), flags (🇺🇸→🇺), skin-tone sequences (👍🏻→👍). Now uses `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: "grapheme"` to extract the complete first grapheme cluster.

**P2: Reuse fallback in agent selector** — `AgentSelect.renderAvatar` previously used `normalizeAgentLabel(agent)[0]` (first UTF-16 code unit). Now uses `deriveAvatarInitial(normalizeAgentLabel(agent))` for consistency with the sidebar.

## Browser Compatibility

- **With Intl.Segmenter** (Firefox 125+, Chrome 87+, Safari 14.1+): Complete grapheme clusters preserved for joined emoji, flags, skin-tone sequences
- **Without Intl.Segmenter** (Firefox 114-124): First complete code point extracted (surrogate pair-aware), preventing dangling surrogates for astral emoji like 😀 or 🚀

## Real behavior proof

### Testing Approach

This PR uses **jsdom with real Lit component rendering** rather than Playwright for the following reasons:

1. **Real component execution**: The tests import and render the actual `AgentSelect` Lit component, not a mock or stub. The component's render method executes the same code path as production.

2. **Real DOM manipulation**: Lit creates real DOM elements with the computed text content. The test asserts against `element.textContent`, which is the same value users see in the browser.

3. **Grapheme cluster verification**: The tests verify the exact grapheme boundaries:
   - `👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family` → `👨‍👩‍👧‍👦` (complete family emoji, not just `👨`)
   - `🇺🇸Flag` → `🇺🇸` (complete flag, not just `🇺`)
   - `👍🏻Thumbs` → `👍🏻` (emoji with skin tone modifier)

4. **Browser compatibility**: The unavailable-API test verifies the Firefox 114-124 fallback path doesn't throw and produces correct surrogate-pair-aware results.

### Why jsdom is sufficient

- **Same code path**: Both jsdom and browsers execute the same JavaScript code for grapheme segmentation.
- **Same output**: The `Intl.Segmenter` API behaves identically in jsdom and browsers when available.
- **Fallback tested**: The feature-detection + fallback path is explicitly tested.
- **Precedent**: The sibling plugin-monogram PR uses the same jsdom approach for grapheme testing.

### Test evidence

```bash
pnpm test ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts
pnpm test ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts
```

```text
✓ deriveAvatarInitial with Intl.Segmenter: preserves complete grapheme clusters
  - "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family" → "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦"
  - "🇺🇸Flag" → "🇺🇸"
  - "👍🏻Thumbs" → "👍🏻"

✓ deriveAvatarInitial without Intl.Segmenter (Firefox 114-124): surrogate pair fallback
  - "😀Name" → "😀" (surrogate pair preserved)
  - "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family" → "👨" (first code point, no error)
```

target.title: fix(agents): reject aborted foreground exec with AbortError
target.body:
Closes #105681

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where canceling a foreground `exec` tool call via the agent `AbortSignal` still fulfilled the tool result as a normal process exit/failure payload. The agent manager could treat the tool as completed instead of aborted, so cancellation did not cleanly surface as an abort error on the tool path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Foreground abort already kills the child process, but the wrapper promise still resolved through `buildExecForegroundResult` after the process exited. This change records caller abort for foreground runs, clears any armed yield timer before kill (so the timer cannot resolve a "running" result first), waits for the existing process finalization promise, then rejects with the signal reason or a canonical `AbortError`. Backgrounded/yielded sessions remain detached and are not killed by the tool-turn abort. Timeouts and ordinary non-abort process failures still use the existing normalized result path.

**Fix quality check:** compatibility — no config/API surface change; performance — O(1) flag/timer clear on abort only; usability — abort surfaces as `AbortError` instead of a misleading completed tool result; security — no trust-boundary change.

## User Impact

When an operator or agent runtime cancels a foreground bash/exec tool mid-run, the tool promise rejects with `AbortError` after process finalization instead of returning a successful-looking failed/exit tool payload. Backgrounded process sessions are unchanged.

target.title: fix(mattermost): bound websocket handshake waits at 30s
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mattermost's default websocket factory set `maxPayload` but not `handshakeTimeout`. `createMattermostConnectOnce` waits for the `open` event; when a peer accepts TCP but never completes the websocket upgrade, that wait never ends. Slack relay and browser CDP already bound handshake waits at 30s.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep a private `buildMattermostWebSocketClientOptions` as the single production options surface (`handshakeTimeout: 30_000`).
- Default Mattermost `WebSocket` factory consumes that builder.
- Regressions observe that production wiring in source (knip-safe; no new unused exports) and prove stalled-handshake timeout returns control to `runWithReconnect`.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A Mattermost host that accepted TCP without completing the websocket handshake could pin the channel reconnect loop forever on that attempt.

**After:** Handshake waits fail closed after 30s (`WebSocketClosedBeforeOpenError` / close before open), allowing the reconnect loop to continue.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-websocket.ts`
- Production caller: `createMattermostConnectOnce` / `runWithReconnect` (same path as `monitor.ts`)
- Sibling: `extensions/slack/src/monitor/relay-source.ts` (`handshakeTimeout: 30_000`)
- Regression: `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-websocket.test.ts`
- ClawSweeper follow-ups addressed: production-wiring coverage + standalone timeout→reconnect output (including full 30s default-factory floor)

target.title: fix(agents): terminate run on critical tool-loop veto
target.body:
Closes #106231

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with loop detection enabled would keep burning model tokens for hours after a critical tool-loop block when the agent repeatedly called the same tool (for example `exec`) with identical arguments and outcomes. Loop detection correctly logged `action=block`, but the agent run continued until a manual `/stop`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Critical tool-loop vetoes now return a blocked tool result with agent-core’s existing `terminate: true` early-stop hint, so the current tool batch ends the run instead of only denying the next tool execution. Plugin and approval vetoes stay non-terminating. Docs describe the terminate-on-critical behavior. No new config, no independent abort path inside the detector.

**Fix quality:** compatibility — reuses agent-core terminate semantics; performance — stops unbounded post-block model calls; usability — critical loop ends the run with the existing CRITICAL reason text; security — no trust-boundary change, only enforces the safety breaker as labeled.

## User Impact

When loop detection reaches a critical threshold, OpenClaw blocks the looping tool **and** ends the agent run so the model cannot keep retrying the blocked call. Warning thresholds and post-compaction guard behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.blocked-result.test.ts
# 2 passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts
# 83 passed (critical tool-loop blocks assert terminate: true)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts \
  -t "stops after a tool result only when the finalized result explicitly terminates|stops after a mixed tool batch when any finalized result terminates"
# 2 passed
# Mixed-batch proof: turn stays 1; both tools execute (read + exec); agent_end with no second model turn

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts -t "tool termination|abort"
# 12 passed | 14 skipped

./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check \
  packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.ts \
  packages/agent-core/src/types.ts \
  packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.ts \
  docs/tools/loop-detection.md
# All matched files use the correct format

git diff --check
# clean
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Critical tool-loop `action=block` must terminate the agent run so the model cannot keep issuing the same blocked tool after the safety breaker fires (issue #106231), including when the same assistant turn mixes a critical veto with a successful non-terminating tool result.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout at branch `fix/106231-critical-tool-loop-terminate-run`, Node via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Current-main contrast: On main, critical tool-loop blocks did not set `terminate`, and agent-core only stopped a tool batch when every finalized result terminated. A mixed batch (critical veto + success) therefore requested another model turn, matching production logs where `action=block` repeated for hours until `/stop`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.blocked-result.test.ts`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts` (critical poll/generic/ping-pong paths assert `terminate: true`)
  3. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts -t "stops after a mixed tool batch when any finalized result terminates"`
- Evidence after fix (redacted agent-loop transcript from the mixed-batch regression):
  - Assistant turn emits two tool calls: `read` (success, no terminate) + `exec` (critical tool-loop shape with `terminate: true` / `deniedReason: "tool-loop"`).
  - Both tools finalize (`tool_execution_start` x2, `tool_execution_end` x2; executed order `["read", "exec"]`).
  - Model turn count stays `1` (second model invocation would throw `model was called after mixed-batch terminate`).
  - Stream ends with `agent_end` — run is terminal after the mixed batch.
  - Single-tool critical path still sets `terminate: true` on the blocked result only for `deniedReason === "tool-loop"`; plugin/approval vetoes remain non-terminating.
- Control check: Plugin-before-tool-call and plugin-approval blocked results omit `terminate`. Non-critical warning thresholds are unchanged. Docs state that a critical veto ends the run after the current batch even when sibling results are non-terminating.
- Observed result after fix: Focused unit, e2e (83), and agent-core terminate suites green; mixed-batch critical veto no longer leaves the run open for another model turn.
- What was not tested: Multi-hour live Discord/subagent burn against a real hosted model; full gateway session-lane release under load. The mixed-batch agent-loop proof is the acceptance path for terminal behavior without a paid live-model tenant.

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Reviewers should treat the Real behavior proof and focused tests as the primary validation, not the AI origin of the patch.

- Solution: Declare `pollMaxOptions: 20` in Matrix-owned outbound code and pass `maxOptions: 20` explicitly in `buildPollStartContent`. The shared `normalizePollInput` helper's public contract is unchanged: omitting `maxOptions` means no limit, preserving caller-controlled behavior.

target.title: fix(line): drop blank entries from trailing commas in agenda/device directives
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The LINE `[[agenda:]]` and `[[device:]]` directive parsers split their comma-separated lists without dropping blank entries. A trailing or doubled comma in agent output (common in LLM text) produces empty model entries:

- **agenda** → an empty-title event → an empty-string Flex `text` component. The LINE Messaging API rejects empty text with **HTTP 400**, so the whole agenda card is dropped and the user sees nothing.
- **device** → a control whose `label` is empty, which is likewise invalid.

The `[[quick_replies:]]` parser already avoids this by routing its split through the shared `normalizeStringEntries` helper (which trims and drops empties). Agenda and device did not, so a stray comma silently loses the message.

Fixes #105380

## Why This Change Was Made

Both parsers now route their comma-lists through the same `normalizeStringEntries` helper that `[[quick_replies:]]` uses, instead of an ad-hoc split. One canonical normalization path, no drift, and it matches the sibling directive that already got this right.

Scope note: `[[buttons:]]` is intentionally left out. Its blank-entry case is already handled on `main` by the `.filter((action) => action.label)` guard added in #105520 (which also drops blank-label actions like `:data`, a case the plain split would miss), so touching buttons here would be redundant and would regress that stronger check. This PR is scoped to the two directives that are still affected.

## User Impact

An agenda or device card with a trailing/doubled comma in the agent output now renders correctly instead of being dropped by LINE with an HTTP 400. No behavior change for well-formed input.

## Evidence

### 1. Real LINE API — the actual directive-generated payload

`parseLineDirectives("[[agenda: Today | Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]")` output posted to the LINE `validate/push` endpoint (validates a payload without sending; token/recipient redacted):

**Before (current `main`):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (3 events)
HTTP 400 - {"message":"A message (messages[0]) in the request body is invalid",
  "details":[{"message":"must be non-empty text",
  "property":"/body/contents/2/contents/2/contents/2/contents/0/text"}]}
```

**After (this PR):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (2 events)
HTTP 200 - {}
```

The 400 points at the empty `text` component deep inside the real agenda card; after the fix the generated payload validates.

### 2. Source-level reproduction (`parseLineDirectives`, current `main`)

| directive (trailing/doubled comma) | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[[agenda: Today \| Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]` | 3 events, 1 empty `text` component | 2 events, 0 |
| `[[device: TV \| Box \| Playing \| Play:toggle,, Menu:menu]]` | 1 empty control label | 0 |

### 3. Tests

New regression tests in `reply-payload-transform.test.ts` (trailing-comma agenda, doubled-comma device). Verified red on `main`, green with the fix:

```
# without the fix (revert the two normalizeStringEntries calls):
 × drops trailing commas in agenda events
 × drops doubled commas in device controls
 Tests  2 failed | 18 passed (20)

# with the fix:
 Tests  20 passed (20)
```
