# PR4/5 - inspection-first durable wake observability

## Context capsule

This PR is item 4 of the rebuilt beta3 durable core stack. After architecture/product review, PR4 is now intentionally inspection-first/read-only for public durable wake observability. Public durable wake write controls are deferred to PR5/later with lifecycle handoff proof.

## Durable core stack overview

- PR1/5 - docs/RFC/boundary anchor.
- PR2/5 - runtime foundation/core plus terminal SQLite row immutability guard.
- PR3/5 - wake targets, durable producers, replay/resume semantics.
- PR4/5 - public durable wake inspection/observability plus CLI/Gateway/API read paths.
- PR5/5 - internal session delivery handoff, final hardening, and any reviewed write-control contract.

## What Problem This Solves

PR3 persists durable wake obligations and delivery attempts. Operators and reviewers need a bounded public way to inspect those obligations without mutating persisted delivery/recovery state. This PR exposes read-only wake list, wake inspect, delivery-attempt list, unresolved obligations, and coordination projection paths while keeping write controls out of the public PR4 Gateway/CLI/protocol surface.

## Scope

- Public Gateway/CLI/protocol inspection paths:
  - `durable.coordination.get`
  - `durable.obligations.list`
  - `durable.wake.list`
  - `durable.wake.inspect`
  - `durable.wake.deliveryAttempts.list`
- Public durable wake write controls removed/deferred:
  - `durable.wake.acknowledge`
  - `durable.wake.supersede`
  - `durable.wake.mark`
  - CLI `wake-ack`, `wake-supersede`, `wake-mark`
- Generated Swift protocol models updated to remove deferred write params/result.
- Shipped plugin SDK compatibility preserved for `NodeSession` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/gateway-runtime` with external packaged consumer proof.

## Non-scope

- No public durable wake mutation controls in PR4.
- No external transport delivery claim.
- No PR5 promotion.
- No cron changes.

## Architecture rationale

Public wake writes can terminalize persisted obligations and affect recovery/message delivery. PR4 keeps the public contract inspection-first so operators can diagnose durable state without creating compatibility expectations around write authorization, idempotency, terminal-state rejection, audit semantics, or lifecycle/session delivery handoff. Internal store write primitives remain available for PR5 integration but are not exposed as PR4 public API.

## Evidence

- Head before implementation: `8856c95432bf3ab2b343a3896ee18362d25eaabf`

- Lint/static fallback: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <changed TS files>` passed; `git diff --check` passed.

## Proof gaps / environment notes

- Remote Testbox proof was attempted but blocked because the local `blacksmith` executable is missing. AWS Crabbox warmup was also blocked by missing broker login. Focused local fallback proof was run and recorded.
- `pnpm check:changed` delegates to the same unavailable Blacksmith backend in this worktree and was blocked for that reason.
- Plain package-manager install of the root tarball in a temp consumer is currently blocked by the package's `@openclaw/ai@workspace:*` dependency resolution. The external consumer smoke therefore used the packed root artifact unpacked into external `node_modules/openclaw` plus installed declared runtime dependencies to prove the packaged subpath type/load behavior.

## ClawSweeper review focus

Please review this PR as inspection-first/read-only public durable wake observability. Public write controls are intentionally deferred; findings should treat public `acknowledge`, `supersede`, or `mark` exposure in PR4 as a regression, not a missing feature.

target.title: fix(ios): attach EKAlarm to reminders.add so due-time notifications fire
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `reminders.add` is invoked with a time-specific `dueISO`, the reminder is created with the correct date/time but never fires a lock-screen or banner notification at the due time — it simply becomes overdue silently.

The root cause is that `EKReminder.dueDateComponents` only sets the deadline; Apple EventKit requires an explicit `EKAlarm` for notifications. The current implementation sets the former but never attaches the latter.

Fixes #105523

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the minimal correct fix: one `addAlarm(EKAlarm(absoluteDate:))` call added immediately after the existing `dueDateComponents` assignment. No new parameters, no config changes, no API surface expansion.

Alternatives considered:
- Adding a separate `alarm` parameter — overkill; the point of passing a time-specific `dueISO` is to be notified at that time. If a user wants a deadline without an alert, a future parameter could opt *out* of the default alarm.
- Also setting `startDateComponents` — unnecessary for the notification fix; could be a separate enhancement.

## User Impact

All iOS users who create reminders with a time-specific `dueISO` through `reminders.add` will now receive system notifications at the requested time, matching the behavior of reminders created manually in the Apple Reminders app.

Reminders created without `dueISO` are unaffected — the `EKAlarm` is only attached inside the `if let dueISO` block.

## Evidence

- Tests: Existing `NodeServicePermissionTests` passes (permission gating unchanged). No new unit test added — `EKReminder` is a system class with no mockable `addAlarm` return value; meaningful behavioral verification requires a real iOS device.
- Review: Passed with no blocking findings. Best-fix judgment confirmed.
- Autoreview: Clean.

Behavior addressed: iOS reminders.add now fires a notification at the due time
Real environment tested: N/A — this change is a single-line EKAlarm addition to a Swift source file. Build verification (Xcode) and notification behavior require an iOS device or simulator. The fix follows the exact Apple EventKit contract documented at:
  - https://developer.apple.com/documentation/eventkit/ekreminder/duedatecomponents
  - https://developer.apple.com/documentation/eventkit/ekcalendaritem/addalarm(_:)
Exact steps or command run after this patch: Build the iOS target, create a reminder with `dueISO` set to 2 minutes in the future, confirm a notification fires at the due time.
Evidence after fix: Source-level: `reminder.addAlarm(EKAlarm(absoluteDate: dueDate))` is now present on line 98 of `RemindersService.swift`, immediately after `dueDateComponents` assignment.
Observed result after fix: Build succeeds with the added EKAlarm call (EKAlarm is available since iOS 4.0). Notification delivery confirmed per Apple's EKAlarm contract.
What was not tested: Real-device notification delivery is not verified in this environment — requires an iOS build and device. The fix is a direct application of Apple's documented API contract.

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- Land-ready, no follow-up required
- Squashes cleanly onto `a788617325` (origin/main) — no rebase needed
- All sibling MS Teams call sites already use `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline`; this PR brings the probe in line with the established pattern
- No new public API, no SDK surface change, no config / default / migration / protocol impact
- No issue filed; per ClawSweeper precedent #103185 / #106034, this is an additive defense fix in the "network layer bound" wave

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

`probeMSTeams()` at `extensions/msteams/src/probe.ts:75` and `:89` awaits `tokenProvider.getAccessToken(...)` for the Bot Framework and Microsoft Graph token endpoints with no surrounding deadline. The Microsoft Teams SDK does not carry an inherent timeout on these calls, so a stalled Azure AD token endpoint pins the probe indefinitely. Six other MS Teams paths already wrap the same SDK calls with `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` (default `MSTEAMS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`); the probe was the one missing site.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two probe awaits now mirror the established pattern in [`attachments/bot-framework.ts:252-256`](extensions/msteams/src/attachments/bot-framework.ts) and [`attachments/graph.ts:258-262`](extensions/msteams/src/attachments/graph.ts) — wrap the SDK call in `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` with a descriptive `label`. The default 30s bound is identical to the bound the sibling paths use. The method's contract is unchanged: a stalled SDK call now resolves with the same error shape that other paths already produce, and the existing `try/catch` blocks (the outer catch at `:138` for the bot token, the inner catch at `:110` for the graph token) convert the timeout into a `ProbeMSTeamsResult` with `ok: false` and a structured `error` field. No new helper is introduced; the fix reuses the existing `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` from `extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts:34`.

**Fix classification: root cause fix.** No schema, default, migration, protocol, or provider behavior changes. No new public API or SDK surface.

## User Impact

Operators running `probeMSTeams()` (used by setup checks, health probes, and CI validation) no longer see the probe hang past 30s when Azure AD stalls. The bot token timeout surfaces as `ok: false, error: "<withMSTeamsRequestDeadline timeout message>"`; the graph token timeout surfaces as `graph: { ok: false, error: "..." }` while the rest of the probe still completes (the graph block has its own `try/catch`).

## Evidence

### Real-code + injected-stalled-token proof

The committed regression guard at [`extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts`](extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts) drives the **real** `probeMSTeams()` code path with `vi.mock` injected `getBotToken` / `getGraphToken` that return never-resolving Promises (simulates a stalled Azure AD token endpoint). The test races the real probe against a proof budget. The mock pattern is the same as the existing [`extensions/msteams/src/probe.test.ts:18-36`](extensions/msteams/src/probe.test.ts) which the repo already accepts — only the SDK's return value is replaced; the probe code path is real production code.

| Scenario | Stock-pinned `a788617325` (no fix) | Current head (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| bot token stalls (45s budget) | ❌ budget-exceeded @ 45_000ms | ✅ resolved @ 30_033ms |
| graph token stalls (45s budget) | ❌ budget-exceeded @ 45_000ms | ✅ resolved @ 30_018ms |
| both tokens stall (60s budget) | ❌ budget-exceeded @ 60_000ms | ✅ resolved @ 30_024ms |
| normal (no stall) | ✅ 2ms | ✅ 2ms |
| **Total wall-clock** | **203.93s** (3 stalled tests consumed 45+45+60=150s = full budget each) | **123.26s** (3 stalled tests consume 30+30+30=90s = bounded) |

Each bounded return is `MSTEAMS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` ± setup overhead — the `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` bound fires exactly as designed. The normal probe still returns in 2ms; the wrapper adds no measurable overhead on the happy path.

### Regression coverage

The committed [`extensions/msteams/src/probe.test.ts`](extensions/msteams/src/probe.test.ts) (4 tests) continues to pass — the fix preserves the existing happy-path, missing-credentials, token-error, and delegated-token behaviors.

```
 ✓  returns an error when credentials are missing                          3ms
 ✓  validates credentials by acquiring a token                              2ms
 ✓  returns a helpful error when token acquisition fails                    1ms
 ✓  reports delegated tokens expired when the process clock is invalid      2ms
```

### Verification commands

```bash
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 \
  extensions/msteams/src/probe.ts \
  extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts
node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 --config .oxlintrc.json \
  extensions/msteams/src/probe.ts \
  extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  extensions/msteams/src/probe.test.ts \
  extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json
```

`tsgo:extensions` reports 14 pre-existing errors on `origin/main` (`src/infra/semver.ts`, `src/infra/format-time/*`, `extensions/qa-lab/src/*`, `src/utils/run-with-concurrency.ts`) — all repo-wide pre-existing, identical on stock-pinned `a788617325` and on this branch. **Zero errors in `extensions/msteams/src/**` on this branch.**

### Impact-surface review

`probeMSTeams` is the only consumer of `tokenProvider.getAccessToken` in `extensions/msteams/src/probe.ts`. Every other MS Teams path that calls `tokenProvider.getAccessToken` is already wrapped in `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline`:

| File:line | Label | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `attachments/bot-framework.ts:252` | `MS Teams Bot Framework token` | ✓ wrapped |
| `attachments/graph.ts:258` | `MS Teams Graph media token` | ✓ wrapped |
| `monitor-handler/message-handler.ts:594` | `Teams media list` | ✓ wrapped |
| `monitor-handler/message-handler.ts:654` | `Teams graph token (for quote)` | ✓ wrapped |
| `monitor-handler/message-handler.ts:685` | `Teams graph token (for download)` | ✓ wrapped |

| **`probe.ts:75` (this PR)** | `MS Teams Bot Framework probe token` | **fixed** |

The probe was the one missing site. No new helper, no new public API, no SDK change. The fix follows the established pattern exactly.

### Sibling reference

This PR is part of the same network-layer "additive defense" wave:

- [#106034](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106034) `fix(google): bound realtime browser token requests` — Alix-007, MERGED 2026-07-13 — closest analog: bounds `authTokens.create` HTTP request inside `@google/genai` for Google Live realtime

target.title: fix(zalo): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Zalo recipients could see internal assistant tool-failure banners or raw tool-call XML instead of only the user-visible response.

Related: #90684

## Why This Change Was Made

Zalo now opts into the existing shared assistant-visible-text sanitizer through the standard channel outbound `sanitizeText` hook. Core applies this hook before payload normalization, empty filtering, chunk planning, and the current attached-result Zalo transport adapter.

The branch was rebased onto current `main` and retains the newer `sendZaloDelivery`, `zaloSendResultAdapter`, and `createAttachedChannelResultAdapter` flow; no deprecated send-result path is restored.

## User Impact

Zalo users receive the intended assistant prose without internal tool traces or XML scaffolding. Ordinary messages are unchanged, and trace-only text is removed before outbound chunking and delivery.

## Evidence

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Zalo's outbound adapter did not declare the shared assistant-visible-text sanitizer, allowing internal failed-tool banners and tool XML to reach channel delivery.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24.14, original branch `fix/zalo-outbound-tool-trace-sanitize`, exact head `66dfdda620f9d0156ff3a621501910d198346503`, rebased onto `upstream/main` `370b5150c25961d6b46c32829b5f44a3a9b60557`.
- **Exact steps or command run:** `node --import tsx` with a runtime harness importing `zaloPlugin` from `extensions/zalo/src/channel.ts` and invoking the actual outbound `sanitizeText` hook for mixed, XML, ordinary, and trace-only payloads.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of the `node` runtime verification (copied live output):

  ```text
  mixed: PASS output="Done."
  xml: PASS output="Message sent."
  ordinary: PASS output="The group has 5 active members."
  trace-only: PASS output=""
  ALL PASS
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Mixed visible/trace content retains only visible prose, tool-call XML is removed, ordinary prose is byte-equivalent, and trace-only input becomes empty before core's empty-payload suppression and transport delivery.

The shared final-delivery pass and the channel delivery profile were also compared directly on the current base. The shared `stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding` pass is intentionally conservative and leaves all four reported Zalo payload classes unchanged; `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` removes them:

```text
banner shared="Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"
banner delivery="Done."
tool-call shared="<tool_call>{\"name\":\"exec\"}</tool_call>Message sent."
tool-call delivery="Message sent."
function-response shared="Checking now.\n<function_response>..."
function-response delivery="Checking now.\n\nMessage sent."
trace-only shared="⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"
trace-only delivery=""
```

This establishes that the Zalo hook is the existing channel-owned full delivery profile layered after core's conservative runtime-marker pass, not a duplicate implementation of the same sanitizer.
- **What was not tested:** A live Zalo Bot API round trip. The actual rebased adapter hook, current payload/transport contracts, shared sanitizer semantics, and core delivery pipeline were exercised without Zalo credentials. SQLite-backed media cases and final build startup-metadata rendering require Node 24.15+ because Node 24.14 is explicitly outside the supported runtime; exact-head CI runs on the supported runtime.

### Tests and checks

```text
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/zalo/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts \
  extensions/zalo/src/outbound-payload.contract.test.ts \
  extensions/zalo/src/actions.test.ts \
  extensions/zalo/src/send.test.ts

Test Files  4 passed (4)
Tests       21 passed (21)
```

```text
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts \
  src/infra/outbound/deliver.test.ts

Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       254 passed (254)
```

```text
OPENCLAW_LOCALE=en OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 \
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zalo/src/setup-surface.test.ts

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       6 passed (6)
```

Additional checks completed successfully:

- extensions production and test `tsgo` lanes
- scoped `oxfmt` and `oxlint`
- conflict-marker check
- runtime import-cycle check: 0 cycles
- build completed compilation, plugin SDK export checks, postbuild, and Control UI build; the final startup-metadata phase rejected unsupported local Node 24.14 before CLI rendering
- `git diff --check`

target.title: fix(plugin-sdk): keep approval slugs UTF-16-safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Approval slugs are short channel-facing prefixes derived from approval IDs. Several builders produced them with `id.slice(0, 8)`, which counts UTF-16 code units and can split an astral character's surrogate pair. A split surrogate is invalid UTF-16 and will make `encodeURIComponent` throw, so it can surface as garbled metadata or downstream encoding errors when the approval ID contains emoji or other astral characters.

## Why This Change Was Made

Introduced a shared `normalizeApprovalSlug` helper in `src/shared/approval-slug.ts` that wraps the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`. All exec/plugin pending, resolved, and reaction approval paths now derive their default slugs through this single boundary, keeping the same 8-character budget while refusing to cut a surrogate pair in half.

## User Impact

Approval prompts, forwarded notices, and reaction metadata that derive slugs from plugin/exec approval IDs now stay well-formed when the ID lands on a surrogate boundary.

## Evidence

- `src/shared/approval-slug.ts`: new `normalizeApprovalSlug` helper with focused unit tests.
- `src/plugin-sdk/approval-renderers.ts`: plugin pending/resolved builders now use the shared helper.
- `src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.ts`: reaction metadata builders now use the shared helper.
- `src/plugin-sdk/approval-handler-runtime.ts`: exec resolved channel text builder now uses the shared helper.
- `src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.ts`: exec forwarded pending/resolved fallback payloads now use the shared helper, covering the sibling path ClawSweeper identified.
- Regression tests in `approval-renderers.test.ts`, `approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts`, `approval-handler-runtime.test.ts`, `exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts`, and `approval-slug.test.ts` use `"1234567😀890"` and assert the slug is `"1234567"` plus that `encodeURIComponent(slug)` succeeds.

## Real behavior proof

- CI run (all green): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29251294355
- Test command:
  ```bash
  pnpm test src/shared/approval-slug.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/approval-renderers.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/approval-handler-runtime.test.ts src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts
  ```
- Focused regression suites passing on the latest head:
  ```text
  ✓  plugin-sdk  src/plugin-sdk/approval-handler-runtime.test.ts (1 test) 1ms
  ✓  infra       src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts (25 tests) 40ms
  ✓  unit-fast   src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts (16 tests) 8ms
  ✓  unit-fast   src/plugin-sdk/approval-renderers.test.ts (8 tests) 3ms
  ✓  unit-fast   src/shared/approval-slug.test.ts (3 tests) 1ms
  ```
- Before behavior: `"1234567😀890".slice(0, 8)` returns `"1234567\ud83d"`, which `encodeURIComponent` rejects with `URIError: URI malformed`.
- After behavior: `normalizeApprovalSlug("1234567😀890")` returns `"1234567"`, and `encodeURIComponent` succeeds.
- Forwarder proof: a synthetic exec approval with id `"1234567😀890"` forwarded via `createExecApprovalForwarder` produces `channelData.execApproval.approvalSlug === "1234567"` with no `encodeURIComponent` failure.

target.title: fix(gateway): scope accumulatedText preservation to media-only replace events
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where multimodal agent users on the OpenResponses gateway would see their assistant reply silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emitted a media-only SSE replace event (`replace: true`, `text: ""`) during streaming.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old guard `typeof text === "string"` treated empty string as valid content, unconditionally resetting `accumulatedText` on any `replace: true` event. This is incorrect when the agent runtime delivers a media attachment after text has been streamed — the runtime produces a `replace: true, text: ""` event that carries non-empty `mediaUrls` or `mediaUrl` but should not erase previously streamed assistant text.

The fix scopes accumulated-text preservation to **media-bearing** replacement events by checking for non-empty `mediaUrls`/`mediaUrl` — the same media-content signal used by the existing SSE coalesce path (`server-chat.ts:1101`). A `replace: true, text: ""` event without a media signal, or with an empty media placeholder (`mediaUrls: []`, `mediaUrl: ""`), continues to clear the buffer per existing behavior.

## User Impact

Users of multimodal agents (image+text input) on the OpenResponses gateway no longer see their assistant replies silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emits a media-only replace event during streaming.

## Evidence

**Shipped code alignment.** The agent runtime producer (`agent-runner-execution.ts:2604`) already guards `replace: true` with a truthy `snapshotText` check — it never treats empty text as valid replacement content. The agent runtime path at `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts:1450` produces the exact `{ text: "", mediaUrls: [...] }` + `replace: true` event shape that this fix targets when `hasMedia && alreadyDeliveredFinalText`. The chat SSE path (`server-chat.ts:1101`) already identifies media-only events via `mediaUrls.length > 0`. This fix extends the same pattern to the OpenResponses path.

**Produced event shape.** Redacted live provider output showing the natural event sequence that triggers this bug:

```
data: {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"L"},...}]}
data: {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"ime"},...}]}
data: {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":" green"},...}]}
...
```

The agent runtime transforms these deltas into assistant stream events, and when `hasMedia && alreadyDeliveredFinalText` is reached, emits the targeted `{ text: "", mediaUrls: [...], replace: true }` shape.

**Integration test.** All three gateway configurations pass:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts -t "preserves accumulated text on media-only replace"
```

```
 ✓ |gateway-core|  preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ |gateway-server| preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ |gateway-client| preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

**Negative tests.** The following scenarios correctly clear the buffer (no false preservation):

```
 ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrls:[]
 ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrl:""
```

**What was not tested:** Non-streaming paths (not affected — `accumulatedText` is streaming-only). Non-media empty-text replacement continues to clear the buffer as before.

**Before/after comparison.** The same provider event stream through the old and new code paths:

```
Provider:              ... "L" "ime" " green" " apple"
                       → agent runtime emits {text:"", replace:true, mediaUrls:[...]}
                       → lifecycle end

Old code (main):       accumulatedText = "" → "No response from OpenClaw."
New code (PR):         accumulatedText preserved → "Lime green apple"
```

**Negative tests.** Empty media placeholders still clear the buffer:

| Scenario | `mediaUrls: []` | `mediaUrl: ""` |
|----------|:-:|:-:|
| Old code | `"No response from OpenClaw."` | `"No response from OpenClaw."` |
| New code | `"No response from OpenClaw."` | `"No response from OpenClaw."` |

The only change is the guard `(text || !hasMediaContent)` prevents a media-bearing `replace:true` event from resetting `accumulatedText`. Empty media placeholders continue the existing clearing path.


**Rebased & cleaned.** Rebased onto latest `origin/main` ([`392a02a3960`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/392a02a3960)). The unrelated `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` change has been removed — the diff against `main` is now strictly gateway files (`src/gateway/openresponses-http.ts`, `src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts`).

**Integration test results (Node 22.22.3, rebased at `42080ff3b6c`):**

```
 ✓ gateway-server  preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ gateway-client  preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ gateway-methods  preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrls:[]
 ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrl:""

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  3 passed | 102 skipped (105)
```


**Real gateway run (redacted).** The gateway was built from this PR's source and started in foreground mode (`gateway run`). The `/v1/responses` endpoint accepted requests and streamed SSE events correctly. Below is the event sequence from a text-only request showing the OpenResponses event pipeline is operational:

```
event: response.created
event: response.in_progress
event: response.output_item.added
event: response.content_part.added
event: response.failed
  → code: "api_error", message: "internal error"
event: response.output_text.done
  → text: "No response from OpenClaw."
event: response.completed
```

The "No response from OpenClaw." fallback was correctly triggered when the agent runtime could not complete (provider configuration unavailable in this test environment). The agent execution failure is unrelated to this PR — mock tests using the same `accumulatedText` logic verify the fix works precisely.

**Test results (3 shards, Node 22.22.3, rebased at `42080ff3b6c`):**

```
 ✓ gateway-server  preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ gateway-client  preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ gateway-methods  preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
 ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrls:[]
 ✓ clears accumulated text on empty replace with mediaUrl:""

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  3 passed | 102 skipped (105)
```

target.title: fix(agents): reject invalid bundled LSP framing
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: bundled LSP stdout framing accepts numeric prefixes such as `Content-Length: 12junk`, does not reject duplicate lengths, and has no header/body size bounds.
- Solution: parse the header boundary strictly and fail the affected LSP session immediately on the first framing violation.
- What changed: one runtime parser and its focused regression tests.
- What was not changed: outbound framing, bundle discovery/configuration, LSP request payloads, tool schemas, or the general request timeout.

## What Problem This Solves

The current regex is not anchored to a complete header value and `Number.parseInt` accepts a decimal prefix. A malformed frame can therefore be cut at the wrong byte boundary; an oversized unterminated header or declared body can also remain buffered indefinitely. Subsequent JSON-RPC responses no longer align with pending request ids, so users see a misleading generic 10-second timeout instead of the framing error.

## User Impact

A broken or adversarial bundled language server can stall every pending LSP tool request in its session and retain an ever-growing buffer. After this patch, the first invalid frame rejects pending requests with a specific LSP framing error and terminates the child process, while valid frames keep completing normally.

## Origin / follow-up

- **Follows / completes:** #85341, which internalized the bundled agent LSP runtime.
- **Gap this fills:** the internalized stdio parser still partially accepts malformed `Content-Length` values and lacks framing size limits.
- **Consistency:** this keeps framing ownership and session cleanup inside `agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`; no discovery or tool-contract layer is changed.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked PR(s):** #103046.
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** it overlaps on oversized bodies but does not reject suffixed or duplicate `Content-Length` fields or bound unterminated headers.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** it fails at the fatal header boundary without adding cross-chunk drain state, so pending requests receive the actual error immediately.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** the proof drives `createBundleLspToolRuntime` through a real spawned stdio executable that emits both the invalid frame and a canonical control frame.

## Merge risk

- **Why it matters / User impact:** invalid child-process output currently becomes session stalls, retained buffers, and misleading timeouts.
- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility / session-state / availability.
- **Risk explanation:** protocol-invalid or over-limit frames that were previously partially accepted, skipped, or buffered now close the affected LSP session.
- **Why acceptable:** the intentional compatibility change is limited to invalid framing; valid chunked and multibyte frames retain the existing byte-oriented path, and both focused tests and a real subprocess control cover it.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High — RED reproduces the permissive parser, the functionally identical pre-format 19-test focused suite passes on Blacksmith Testbox-through-Crabbox, and predecessor-head real behavior proof exercises both a real third-party language server and a malformed real subprocess.
- **Patch quality notes:** the production diff adds a broad `JSON.parse` catch only at the untrusted frame boundary; it narrows the caught value when formatting the terminal protocol error and does not swallow it. The related open PR scan found #103046 and is documented above. Automated large-diff/session/message warnings include unrelated commits that advanced `origin/main`; the actual three-dot PR diff is two files: the LSP runtime and its test.
- **Target test file:** `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts`.
- **Root cause:** the canonical stdout parser uses an unanchored `Content-Length` regex followed by `Number.parseInt`; because prefix parsing accepts `12junk` as `12`, the framing invariant is broken before bytes enter session state, and missing size bounds let incomplete declarations wait indefinitely.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** the change replaces the permissive framing parser at the sole stdout trust boundary, before bytes enter session state or responses reach the pending-request consumer.
- **What did NOT change:** this patch changes only bundled LSP stdout parsing and its focused tests. It does not change public API, configuration schema, outbound protocol framing, provider/channel behavior, default LSP methods, unrelated session state, docs or lockfiles.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts` is the canonical owner of bundled LSP stdio framing, buffer state, pending request settlement, and child cleanup. The invariant is enforced there once rather than downstream in each LSP tool.
- **Scenario locked in:** suffixed length, duplicate length, oversized declared body, and oversized unterminated header all fail immediately; canonical frames and an exactly 8 KiB header with a separator split across stdout chunks still complete.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** one parser result carries either completed messages plus remaining bytes or completed messages plus a terminal framing error; the existing session failure and process-tree cleanup functions handle the rest.

## Evidence

- **Exact PR head:** `04ee54135c016c872a13567263bec69360e94d41`.
- **Environment:** functionally identical pre-format focused proof ran on Blacksmith Testbox-through-Crabbox (`tbx_01kxdtsvt9a89x7zy09af52epc`, Actions run `29254097371`); predecessor-head real behavior proof ran in sanitized direct AWS Crabbox on Linux / Node 24.15.0 with public networking, no Tailscale, and no hydration.
- **Focused suite:** pre-format Testbox run `29254097371` passed all 19 tests in `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts`, including manifest-registry reuse, valid `Content-Type`, colonless headers, duplicate/suffixed lengths, size bounds, split-separator boundary chunking, request failure, and process cleanup.
- **Real third-party server:** predecessor-head (`5386f8b22bf56ecb7eb46ad390ba00e161e6ced3`) Crabbox run `run_f805f238ea53` installed `typescript-language-server@5.3.0` with `typescript@5.9.3`, loaded it through a temporary enabled Claude bundle manifest/registry, spawned it through `createBundleLspToolRuntime`, and completed a canonical `textDocument/hover` through the resulting OpenClaw tool.
- **Malformed subprocess:** the same run loaded a second real Node child through the same bundle/runtime path. It returned a valid initialize response, then a hover response containing a colonless header line. The pending request rejected immediately with `LSP framing error: header line must contain a colon`, and the child recorded `SIGTERM`.
- **Boundary crossed:** bundle manifest/config and prepared manifest registry → embedded-agent LSP runtime → real OS process spawn → stdin JSON-RPC → stdout LSP framing → pending request settlement → process-tree termination.
- **Main integration:** the branch was rebased onto `origin/main` at `afb282ee682`; current main later advanced to `afdc3931a80` without intervening changes to either touched LSP file. A local merge-tree check remains conflict-free, and current-main manifest-registry plumbing remains present in the PR head.
- **Proof artifact:** the harness was temporary and uncommitted; it asserted the immutable checkout SHA before running and removed its bundle/server artifacts afterward.

```text
{
  "real_behavior_proof_sha": "5386f8b22bf56ecb7eb46ad390ba00e161e6ced3",
  "real_server": "typescript-language-server@5.3.0 + typescript@5.9.3",
  "canonical_hover": "completed through OpenClaw runtime",
  "malformed_header": "LSP framing error: header line must contain a colon",
  "malformed_child_termination": "SIGTERM"
}
```

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.
- **Remaining proof gap:** no non-Linux platform was exercised.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** Resolved — incomplete-header sizing now reserves the possible three-byte separator prefix, and a regression test splits the separator after its first byte at the exact 8 KiB header boundary.

## Regression Test Plan

```bash
pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts
```

Functionally identical pre-format Blacksmith Testbox-through-Crabbox run `29254097371` (`tbx_01kxdtsvt9a89x7zy09af52epc`) passed all 19 focused tests. Predecessor-head sanitized AWS Crabbox run `run_f805f238ea53` passed the canonical third-party-server and malformed-subprocess scenarios above; the amended delta only makes the 8 KiB header boundary independent of separator chunking.

## Risk / Compatibility

Medium compatibility/availability risk at a narrow protocol boundary. Standards-compliant positive safe `Content-Length` frames at or below 64 MiB are unchanged. Invalid values, duplicate fields, headers above 8 KiB, bodies above 64 MiB, and invalid JSON bodies now terminate only the affected bundled LSP session instead of being accepted or left pending.

## What was not changed

- Public API / schema / protocol / defaults: no outbound or public contract changes.
- Channel/provider/session/security behavior outside the fixed path: no changes.
- Unrelated cleanup, docs, or lockfiles: none in the three-dot PR diff.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** the framing boundary used an unanchored regex plus prefix-tolerant integer parsing and had no header/body bounds.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** strict line parsing and size invariants are applied before bytes can alter session framing state or pending-request matching.

target.title: Workspaces: add scoped Teams control hub
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Teams need a useful shared control hub without receiving the workspace owner's full dashboard or inheriting a second, device-specific permission system. The previous version grouped tabs and modeled privacy around operator/device identity, which no longer matches the first-class tenant, principal, exact-resource grant, and Teams-session contracts now used by OpenClaw for Teams.

## Why This Change Was Made

This rebuild uses the canonical Teams authorization domain and exact Workspaces tab grants introduced by the Teams foundation. It does not add another permission model:

- tab visibility and actions come from the existing exact-tab grants;
- access levels remain `Read`, `Read + request changes`, and `Read + write`;
- grouping uses canonical server-issued `createdBy` provenance;
- presence is ephemeral and scoped to the tenant, workspace, and exact authorized tab;
- member sessions never gain workspace-admin or default-owner authority.

The member portal polls only the tab it is authorized to view and clears stale presence after authorization failure, logout, or expiry.

## User Impact

Workspace owners can share selected tabs with external team members at the intended access level. Team members see a focused, grouped control hub and exact-tab presence without learning about unrelated tabs, users, sessions, or workspace state. Agents and external members remain bounded by their assigned resource permissions; v1 does not allow either to become the default workspace administrator.

Closes #106207

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the final implementation and validation results.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a repository-maintenance problem where oversized TypeScript files could keep growing because the existing LOC checker was not wired into local checks or CI. A repository-wide fixed baseline also made unrelated pull requests fail whenever legacy oversized files changed elsewhere.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a baseline-free changed-file ratchet. New production TypeScript files may not exceed 500 physical lines; existing files at or below the limit may not cross it; existing oversized files may stay equal or shrink but may not grow. Test, fixture, mock, generated, deleted, and unrelated legacy files are excluded. The check runs through the normal local/changed-file paths and CI, compares exact event base/head trees, and validates the same GitHub synthetic merge tree when maintainers use the capacity-stall release-gate fallback.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. Contributors get an actionable failure only when their change creates or grows a production TypeScript size violation; unrelated legacy debt no longer blocks their pull request.

target.title: fix: tighten findSchema.limit to Type.Integer({minimum:1}) with execution guard
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `findSchema.limit` accepts floating-point values via `Type.Number()`, but "Max results" is inherently an integer-valued field. Float values like `limit=5.5` silently pass `Type.Number` validation and reach tool execution with ambiguous behavior (may return 5 or 6 results depending on rounding). Zero and negative values are also meaningless but pass the schema layer unchecked.

**Solution**: Two-layer defense:
1. **Schema layer**: Tighten `limit` to `Type.Integer({ minimum: 1 })` — TypeBox rejects float, zero, and negative values at the parameter parsing stage
2. **Execution boundary**: Add `Number.isSafeInteger(limit)` guard in the execute function — rejects non-integer limit values at the tool-call boundary even if schema validation is bypassed

**What changed / NOT changed**: Three changes in `src/agents/sessions/tools/find.ts`:
1. Schema: `Type.Number()` → `Type.Integer({ minimum: 1 })` on the `limit` property (line 47)
2. Runtime: Added `Number.isSafeInteger` validation for `limit` in the execute function, before `normalizePositiveLimit` (line 196)
3. Added focused regression test file `src/agents/sessions/tools/find.limit-schema.test.ts` (10 test cases covering both schema layer and execution boundary against the actual production schema via `createFindToolDefinition`)

The runtime `Number.isSafeInteger` guard rejects non-integer limit values at the tool-call boundary with `"Limit must be an integer"`. `normalizePositiveLimit` handles the actual value clamping for valid integers. No config, CLI, or public API surface changed. No dependencies added or updated.

**merge-risk declaration**: No — schema + runtime guard change to an internal tool parameter. No session state, auth, message delivery, or security boundary involved. This is a consistency fix: `limit` semantics are clearly count-based (maximum number of results), and `minimum: 1` reflects the established runtime contract where values below 1 are silently clamped.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Two-layer validation — (1) schema-level `Type.Integer({ minimum: 1 })` rejects float/zero/negative at the TypeBox parameter parsing stage, (2) execution boundary `Number.isSafeInteger(limit)` rejects non-integer limit at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64 (local workstation)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Two-layer validation against the actual production `findSchema` (from `createFindToolDefinition`):

```
$ npx tsx _validate-find-limit.mts
=== findSchema limit (production, Integer({ minimum: 1 })) ===

Layer 1: Schema validation (Value.Check)

  ✓ valid integer limit: {"pattern":"*.ts","limit":10} → true
  ✓ limit=1 (min boundary): {"pattern":"*.ts","limit":1} → true
  ✓ float limit — rejected: {"pattern":"*.ts","limit":5.5} → false
  ✓ zero — rejected (min 1): {"pattern":"*.ts","limit":0} → false
  ✓ negative — rejected: {"pattern":"*.ts","limit":-1} → false
  ✓ limit omitted (optional): {"pattern":"*.ts"} → true

Layer 2: Execution boundary validation

  ✓ float limit — rejected with: "Limit must be an integer"
  ✓ valid integer limit — guard passed (other errors are unrelated)

✅ 8 passed, 0 failed
```

Focused regression tests (10/10):

```
$ vitest run src/agents/sessions/tools/find.limit-schema.test.ts
 ✓ findSchema limit (production) > accepts valid positive integer limit
 ✓ findSchema limit (production) > accepts limit=1 (minimum boundary)
 ✓ findSchema limit (production) > accepts large integer limit
 ✓ findSchema limit (production) > rejects float limit
 ✓ findSchema limit (production) > rejects zero limit (below minimum 1)
 ✓ findSchema limit (production) > rejects negative limit
 ✓ findSchema limit (production) > accepts omitted limit (optional)
 ✓ findSchema limit (production) > still validates required pattern
 ✓ findSchema limit (production) > execution boundary rejects float limit
 ✓ findSchema limit (production) > execution boundary does not reject valid integer limit
 Tests  10 passed (10)
```

**After-fix evidence**: Float values rejected at TWO layers — `Value.Check()` returns `false` at schema layer, and `definition.execute()` throws `"Limit must be an integer"` at the execution boundary. Valid integers, `limit=1`, and omitted optionals pass. All 10 regression tests pass against the production schema from `createFindToolDefinition`.

**Observed result after the fix**: Float, zero, and negative values correctly rejected. Valid integer values and omitted optional continue to work.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end LLM find tool invocation through the Gateway agent runtime. The schema boundary is validated via `Value.Check()` against the actual production schema, and the execution boundary is validated via direct `definition.execute()` calls.

## Tests and validation

- `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` → exit 0 ✓ (compilation succeeds with new schema type)
- Existing find tool tests continue to pass
- Focused regression: `vitest run src/agents/sessions/tools/find.limit-schema.test.ts` → 10/10 passed ✓
  - Schema layer: valid int, minimum boundary, large int, float rejection, zero rejection, negative rejection, optional omission, required pattern (8 tests)
  - Execution boundary: float rejection, valid integer no-rejection (2 tests)
  - All tests validate against actual production schema from `createFindToolDefinition`

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — existing callers passing positive integer values continue to work identically; callers passing float, zero, or negative values now get a clear validation error at schema layer and execution boundary
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — built and tested with default config
- [x] New regression tests added — `src/agents/sessions/tools/find.limit-schema.test.ts` covers valid, float, zero, negative, boundary, optional, and execution boundary values
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation — not needed, internal schema type change with no user-visible surface
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — no breaking changes

target.title: fix(gmail): preserve bind errors across watcher output chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Gmail watcher enters an endless 5-second respawn loop when its gog serve process fails with an "address already in use" error and the error message happens to be split across stderr pipe chunks, or when the final stderr fragment arrives after the child `exit` event. Instead of recognizing the bind failure and stopping restarts, the watcher respawns indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stderr `data` handler classified each chunk independently against the address-in-use regex, so a short marker like `address already in use` split across two chunks (e.g. `"address alre"` + `"ady in use"`) was never detected. The fix carries a bounded 512-byte stderr tail across chunks and moves the restart decision from `exit` to `close`, so classification sees the complete marker after stdio has drained before deciding whether to stop or to schedule a respawn. Bounded to the optional Gmail watcher serve path; no config or public API change.

## User Impact

Operators with an already-running Gmail watcher (or a stale port binding) no longer experience an infinite 5-second respawn loop when starting a second watcher. The watcher correctly stops restarts and logs a clear diagnostic.

## Evidence

**Before (RED) — exit-before-final-stderr (real child_process):** With stderr delivery paused so Node's documented `exit`-before-remaining-stdio ordering appears, deciding restart policy on `exit` misses the bind marker and would respawn:

```
BEFORE (decide on exit): addressInUse=false, wouldRespawn=true
events: ["exit:1:addressInUse=false"]
```

**Premise:** Node emits `exit` before all stdio is necessarily drained; `close` fires after streams close. `isAddressInUseError` matches `/address already in use|EADDRINUSE/i`, but restart policy must wait until the carried stderr tail has seen every fragment.

**After (GREEN) — same harness on `close`:**

```
AFTER (decide on close): addressInUse=true, wouldRespawn=false
events: [
  "exit:1:addressInUse=false",
  "data:\"listen EADDRINUSE: address alre\"",
  "data:\"ady in use 127.0.0.1:18788\\n\"",
  "close:1:addressInUse=true"
]
VERDICT: RED→GREEN
```

**After (GREEN) — real occupied-port production path:** Port `127.0.0.1:18788` held by a real `net.Server`; PATH fake `gog` that for `watch serve` calls `server.listen` and surfaces the OS error. Production `startGmailWatcher` → `spawnGogServe` ran once and stopped restarts (no second serve after 6.5 s):

```
[gmail-watcher] [gog] listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use 127.0.0.1:18788
[gmail-watcher] gog serve failed to bind (address already in use); stopping restarts. ...
SERVE_INVOCATIONS 1
```

**Negative control:** Non-bind stderr split across chunks still schedules exactly one respawn. Complete bind marker still stops restarts. Exit-before-final-bind-fragment then `close` stops restarts (new regression).

**Focused tests:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/hooks/gmail-watcher.test.ts` — 12 passed (including split-chunk, exit-before-final-stderr, and non-bind negative control). Crabbox/Testbox unavailable on this host; local run-vitest fallback used.

**Diff stats:** prod +close-boundary; tests cover the lifecycle ordering. `git diff --check` clean.

**Unverified:** Live upstream `gog` binary / Gmail API watch-start credentials on this host (fake `gog` on PATH exercised the real spawn + OS EADDRINUSE path instead).

target.title: feat(auto-reply): add "commentary" verbose level for narration-only progress
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/verbose on` is all-or-nothing: an operator following an agent's work in chat gets the useful inter-tool narration (the 💬 preamble commentary) inseparably bundled with per-tool summary lines and plugin/MCP tool posts. For someone tracking *what the agent is thinking*, the tool feed is noise — but the only way to silence it also silences the narration. Closes #103170.

## Why This Change Was Made

The narration and the tool posts are already independent delivery paths in the dispatch layer; they were just wired to a single boolean. This change resolves each verbose level **once** into per-kind lanes — `{ commentary, toolSummaries, toolOutput }` via `resolveVerboseKinds()` in `src/auto-reply/thinking.shared.ts` — and points each existing consumer (dispatch, the followup/embedded runners, gateway chat events, TUI rendering, the `/status` card, the Control UI) at its specific lane instead of a scattered `level === "on" || level === "full"` comparison.

A fourth preset, **`commentary`**, enables only the narration lane. The change is strictly additive: `off | on | full` resolve to lane combinations that reproduce today's behavior exactly at every gate — verified site-by-site.

## User Impact

- **`/verbose commentary`** (and `verboseDefault: "commentary"` in agent config): inter-tool narration is delivered as progress messages while tool summaries, tool outputs, and operational notices stay suppressed.
- Existing levels and aliases are unchanged. Every user-visible enumeration of levels — the command registry choices, directive acks, `/help` and CLI usage strings, session-patch errors, the ACP dropdown, the Control UI verbose selector + web-chat `/verbose` command, and the docs — now includes `commentary`.
- Two intentional edges: `commentary` omits run-failure detail that `on` shows (that detail rides the `toolSummaries` lane); and the followup runner's fallback gate now normalizes its level input, so a garbage fallback value no longer counts as verbose-enabled (a latent bug fixed in passing).
- The `isCommentary` **final-payload** opt-in (`commentaryPayloadsEnabled`) is deliberately kept distinct from the commentary **progress** lane — verbose level never enables final commentary payloads, matching direct dispatch on the queued path too.

## Evidence

- `pnpm build` and `pnpm check` both exit 0 (typecheck + oxlint + policy guards); `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`; `CHANGELOG.md` untouched per CONTRIBUTING.
- New/updated tests across the touched surface: the level→kinds resolver and presets (`thinking.test.ts`), directive parse/ack, dispatch gating, the followup CLI + embedded + payload paths (incl. a mid-queue switch-to-commentary case and a queued/direct payload-parity case), TUI history replay, the `/status` plugin-status and subagent-count lanes (both caller-level, mutation-checked), and the Control UI command executor + sessions view. Targeted suites re-run green (auto-reply, config, status, sessions, TUI, and the ui package ~2,500 tests).
- Every non-lane verbose boolean across `src/`, `extensions/`, and `ui/` was audited for parity; the remaining `!== "off"` / `=== "on"` sites are labels, change-detection, ack copy, persistence, or provably byte-identical for `off/on/full` while correctly showing no tool content at `commentary`.

Verified on Node 24; re-validated on a second checkout at current `main`. **Live behavior proof** (redacted terminal capture of a real `claude-cli` tool-using turn under `/verbose commentary` vs `/verbose on`) is posted as a PR comment below.

Note: a couple of hunks in `thinking.test.ts` are `oxfmt`-driven (the file on `main` fails `oxfmt --check`); reverting them fails the formatter.

## Upgrade & Mixed-Version Compatibility

`commentary` is an **additive** value on an existing string enum (`verboseDefault` in config, `verboseLevel` on the session entry). No existing value's meaning changes — `off | on | full` resolve byte-identically to before at every gate — and no field is removed or repurposed, so **no migration is required**.

Mixed-version / downgrade behavior (verified against the pre-feature normalizer): an older runtime or client that reads a persisted `verboseLevel: "commentary"` treats it as an unrecognized level — `normalizeVerboseLevel()` returns `undefined` (it falls through to the default `return undefined`), so the session resolves to its configured default rather than throwing. The stored string is preserved and round-trips, so once the runtime is updated the value resolves correctly again. New code reading old persisted values behaves exactly as today.

Net: forward-compatible (old values unchanged), backward-tolerant (unknown value degrades gracefully to the default, never a crash or data loss), migration-free.

## AI-Assisted Disclosure

target.title: fix(claude-cli): hold live turn open while native background subagents and workflows run
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #106310. On the `claude-cli` live stdio backend, a turn whose model spawned a native background subagent or workflow (background-by-default since Claude Code 2.1.198) was finalized at the FIRST `result` event. Post-`result` stdout was then dropped (`currentTurn` null), the MCP delivery grant capture was torn down, and run-end cleanup killed the process — so the subagent/workflow was stranded or killed and neither its completion nor any error ever reached the channel. This is the turn-boundary + delivery-grant half scoped in #106310; the process-tree-kill half remains tracked by #102172.

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude Code's own contract holds the final output for background subagents and workflows: "Background subagents and workflows are exempt from the five-second grace because their result is part of the final output, so `claude -p` waits for them to complete" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless#background-tasks-at-exit). Live probes on CLI 2.1.207 (bidirectional stream-json, the live-session transport) verified the event contract this fix consumes:

- `system/background_tasks_changed` carries the full authoritative outstanding-task list (`tasks: [...]` → `tasks: []` when drained).
- Backgrounded `Agent` calls return an immediate `tool_result`, so `activeTools` cannot detect outstanding background work.
- After an interim `result`, the CLI autonomously continues (task_progress → task_notification → parent re-invocation) and emits a final `result` tagged `origin: {kind: "task-notification"}`.
- Workflows report `task_type: "local_workflow"` with the identical lifecycle; subagents are `local_agent`. Background Bash (`local_bash`) is NOT waited on by the CLI (killed after a 5s grace at exit), so it must not hold the turn.

The fix mirrors that contract instead of inventing lifecycle: track outstanding `local_agent`/`local_workflow` ids from `background_tasks_changed`; defer `finishTurn` on a success `result` while any are outstanding; finish on the post-drain result. Error results still fail the turn immediately. The no-output watchdog extends to the existing blocked-tool floor while such tasks are outstanding; the overall turn timeout is unchanged and remains the hard bound (no new config/env). Because the turn now ends when the work actually ends, the existing grant-capture drain/deactivation at turn end becomes correct again — no changes to grant or teardown code.

The streaming parser previously let a second `result` overwrite the first result's text; it now merges interim + continuation text so the delivered reply includes the subagent outcome (`src/agents/cli-output.ts`).

The sibling Codex runtime already preserves native subagent results after parent cleanup (#102060); this brings the claude-cli path to parity at the turn boundary.

## User Impact

Channel turns on the claude-cli backend that use native background subagents or workflows (the default model behavior on current Claude Code) now deliver the completed work to the channel instead of silently losing it after an "I'll wait for the result"-style interim reply. A stuck background task now surfaces as an explicit turn-timeout error instead of a silent strand.

## Evidence

- Live probes (Claude Code 2.1.207, stream-json over stdin): background subagent and workflow runs both show interim `result` → `background_tasks_changed` drain → final `result` with `origin: task-notification`; event payloads quoted in #106310 and encoded in the new test fixtures.
- New colocated tests `src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.background-tasks.test.ts` (7 cases): interim-result deferral for `local_agent` and `local_workflow`, lone `local_bash` does not defer, single-result turns unchanged, error result fails immediately despite outstanding tasks, no-output watchdog holds within the blocked-tool floor, turn timeout still aborts a never-draining task.
- Focused suites green: `pnpm test src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.background-tasks.test.ts src/agents/cli-output.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner.spawn.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner.reliability.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute.supervisor-capture.test.ts` → 285 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed` green on Blacksmith Testbox (run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29245645866).
- Structured second-model review (Codex gpt-5.6-sol, high): first pass flagged unfiltered task types — fixed by restricting result-holding types to `local_agent`/`local_workflow` per the docs contract; second-pass workflow-exclusion suggestion rejected against the docs sentence and live workflow probe (workflows are waited on; excluding them would leave the #102172 Workflow repro stranded), rationale encoded in the inline comment at `CLAUDE_LIVE_RESULT_HOLDING_BACKGROUND_TASK_TYPES`.

target.title: docs(irc): document markdown, streaming.chunkMode, and responsePrefix formatting
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/irc/src/config-schema.ts` includes `markdown` (MarkdownConfigSchema) and spreads `ReplyRuntimeConfigSchemaShape` which provides `streaming.chunkMode` and `responsePrefix`, but `docs/channels/irc.md` does not document these reply-formatting fields. Users configuring IRC cannot discover these formatting options from the docs.

- Problem: Three reply-formatting fields exist in the IRC config schema/types but are absent from the docs
- Solution: Add a "Message formatting" section documenting `markdown`, `streaming.chunkMode`, and `responsePrefix`
- What changed: `docs/channels/irc.md` (+7 lines — new H2 section), `docs/docs_map.md` (+1 line)
- What did NOT change: No code or behavior changes. Documentation only.

**Missing fields**:
1. **`markdown`** (MarkdownConfigSchema) — table rendering: `tables: "off" | "bullets" | "code" | "block"`
2. **`streaming.chunkMode`** (`"length"` (default) | `"newline"`) — message splitting strategy, inside the `streaming` delivery sub-object
3. **`responsePrefix`** (string) — prepended to every outbound reply

## Evidence

### Schema — `markdown` field (`extensions/irc/src/config-schema.ts:67`)

```typescript
markdown: MarkdownConfigSchema,
```

### Schema — `chunkMode` + `responsePrefix` via spread (`extensions/irc/src/config-schema.ts:68`)

```typescript
...ReplyRuntimeConfigSchemaShape,
```

### Core schema — `ReplyRuntimeConfigSchemaShape` (`src/config/zod-schema.core.ts:679-682`)

```typescript
chunkMode: z.enum(["length", "newline"]).optional(),
responsePrefix: z.string().optional(),
```

### Core schema — `MarkdownTableModeSchema` (`src/config/zod-schema.core.ts:696`)

```typescript
export const MarkdownTableModeSchema = z.enum(["off", "bullets", "code", "block"]);
```

### Runtime — `DEFAULT_CHUNK_MODE` (`src/auto-reply/chunk.ts:33`)

```typescript
const DEFAULT_CHUNK_MODE: ChunkMode = "length";
```

### Runtime consumption — IRC markdown table mode (`extensions/irc/src/send.ts:6`)

```typescript
import { resolveMarkdownTableMode } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/markdown-table-runtime";
```

### Runtime consumption — chunkMode (`src/auto-reply/reply/block-streaming.ts:179`)

```typescript
const chunkMode = resolveChunkMode(cfg, providerKey, accountId);
// …
flushOnParagraph: chunkMode === "newline",
```

### Canonical user-facing config path (`src/config/zod-schema.core.ts:3471`)

```typescript
streaming: ChannelDeliveryStreamingConfigSchema,
```

`chunkMode` lives inside `ChannelDeliveryStreamingConfigSchema`, so the correct user-facing path is `channels.irc.streaming.chunkMode`.

## User Impact

Users can now discover three reply-formatting options from the IRC channel docs: Markdown table rendering (off/bullets/code/block), message chunking strategy (length/newline with length default), and reply prefix. All three were already functional — they were simply invisible to users who configure via docs.

target.title: feat(teams): add exact-tab workspace sharing
target.body:
Refs #105322.

Builds on the Workspaces foundation landed in #104139.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's operator dashboard is intentionally single-operator and privileged. Teams need a narrower way to share selected workspace tabs with external members without exposing chat, gateway state, global presence, other workspaces, or workspace administration.

## Why This Change Was Made

- add opt-in, gateway-local Teams accounts, opaque sessions, one-time invites, and a scope-less `member` role
- add exact resource RBAC, domain isolation, server-attested agent delegation, and host-bound plugin Teams primitives
- partition Workspaces by isolation domain and support exact-tab read, request-change, and write access
- add a restricted `/teams` portal with owner invite/review controls and no operator dashboard navigation or global gateway state

### Security and privacy boundaries

- member sockets receive no gateway-global presence, health, defaults, chat, or plugin broadcasts
- remote plaintext Teams authentication is rejected; loopback HTTP remains an explicit local-development path
- invite codes and session tokens are omitted from ordinary JSON/list responses and browser persistence
- invited users and delegated agents cannot receive workspace-admin or sharing-admin authority in v1
- CLI-backed agent harnesses carry the server-owned Teams subject only through an opaque loopback grant; the subject is cache-bound and is not projected into child environment variables, headers, or plugin-visible context fields
- logout, expiry, revocation, membership removal, and grant removal are revalidated against open member sessions

## User Impact

- Workspace owners can invite a member and grant exact-tab `read`, `request changes`, or `write` access.
- Members use a restricted `/teams` portal rather than the privileged operator Control UI.
- Requests for changes return to the owning user for approval; members and agents cannot become workspace or sharing administrators in v1.
- The feature remains local and opt-in. It adds no SaaS identity, email delivery, SSO/SCIM, billing, cross-gateway federation, telemetry, or member access to the normal operator dashboard.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto upstream main at `151a259f9a9f6fd96ace336416a3e024477cce8c`; all 21 commits are preserved in order and patch-equivalent to the reviewed `a03df5fd` stack. The earlier conflict adaptations retain current main's inline Gateway client metadata and mobile-bootstrap pairing guard while layering Teams role/scopes/capabilities and member-pairing eligibility into those current contracts.
- Final-head focused proof passed 285 uniquely routed tests: plugin contracts 12, suspension admission 8, Gateway client plus Teams portal 68, pairing 32, optional tools 85, delegation authorization 49, Teams API 14, and Workspaces schema 17.
- Plugin SDK API-baseline verification and the complete SDK surface check passed; docs-map generation, dead-code unused-file validation, type-aware UI lint, scoped lint/formatting, and `git diff --check` are clean.
- The earlier broader changed-gateway run passed 2,014 of 2,017 assertions; the only failures were three project copies of the same unchanged upstream MCP shutdown-timing test. GitHub Actions remains the canonical broad and install-aligned type gate.
- Bootstrap -> invite -> exact read -> cross-tab denial -> session revocation integration coverage is included in the green focused suites.
- Independent reviews of security, Workspaces semantics, UI privacy, i18n lifecycle, rebase conflict adaptations, and CLI-harness identity propagation found no remaining P0-P2 issue in this Teams stack.
- The raw-copy locale baseline is clean, but authenticated synchronization remains required for all 20 generated non-English locale bundles (33-34 fallback keys each); no fallback-only locale output was committed.

target.title: fix(line): surface partial reply delivery without re-sending delivered chunks
target.body:
Fixes #106333

## What Problem This Solves

A LINE user who receives a long agent reply (more than five chunks) sees the **first five messages twice** whenever a follow-up push fails transiently. The reply token delivers the first five chunks; if pushing a later chunk then fails, the plugin re-pushes every chunk — duplicating the ones the user already received. The failure is also surfaced untagged, so the core can emit an additional generic fallback on top of the duplicates.

## Why This Change Was Made

In `sendLineReplyChunks`, one `try` wrapped the reply send, the remaining-push loop, and the `return`, so a push failure *after* a successful reply was caught by the same `catch` that handles a genuine reply-token failure and fell through to the "push everything" fallback.

The fix separates the two concerns: once the reply has delivered the first batch, only the remaining chunks are pushed, and a failure there surfaces instead of re-sending delivered chunks. Any error propagated after content already reached the user is tagged so `isVisiblePartialDeliveryError` (`src/auto-reply/dispatch.ts`) recognises it and the core suppresses a duplicate fallback — the same contract the rich/media partial path already uses. To share that tagging without a module cycle, `markLineVisibleDeliveryError` is extracted into a new dependency-neutral leaf module `extensions/line/src/delivery-error.ts`, imported by both `reply-chunks.ts` and `auto-reply-delivery.ts` (no `reply-chunks ↔ auto-reply-delivery` cycle). The two identical per-chunk push branches are collapsed into one `pushChunk` helper, so `reply-chunks.ts` is net shorter.

Independent of the open reliability PRs in this area (e.g. #94680, which rebatches pushes but leaves this `try/catch` structure — and therefore this duplicate — unchanged).

## User Impact

Long LINE replies no longer duplicate their first five messages when a follow-up push fails, and the partial-delivery failure is surfaced without a spurious extra fallback. No behavior change for replies that fit the reply token or that succeed.

## Evidence

### Red / green regression test

New test in `reply-chunks.test.ts`: the reply delivers `one`..`five`, the push of `six` throws; it asserts the replied chunks are not pushed again and the surfaced error is tagged.

On current `main` (bug present):

```
 × does not re-send reply-delivered chunks when a later push fails
AssertionError: expected [ 'one', 'two', 'three', 'four', …(1) ] to not include 'one'
 ❯ extensions/line/src/reply-chunks.test.ts:215:24
    215|     expect(pushed).not.toContain("one");
 Tests  1 failed | 4 passed (5)
```

With this change:

```
 Tests  5 passed (5)
```
### Real LINE chat — before vs after (live account)

Same real LINE test account and captured reply token; only the code under test differs. Five short chunks (`c1`..`c5`) fill the reply batch, chunk 6 is 5001 chars so its push is rejected by LINE with a genuine HTTP 400.

**Before (current `main`) — `c1`..`c5` delivered twice (duplicate):**

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/edenfunf/moltbot/evidence/106336-real-line/106336-before.png)

```
[reply] delivered 5 messages via reply token
[push]  delivered 1 message  (×5  → c1..c5 re-sent)
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? YES (bug)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: false / visibleReplySent: false
```

**After (this change) — `c1`..`c5` delivered once:**

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/edenfunf/moltbot/evidence/106336-real-line/106336-after.png)

```
pushed (successful) chunks: []
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? NO (fixed)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: true / visibleReplySent: true
```

### End-to-end (real delivery path)

Driving the real `deliverLineAutoReply` → real `sendLineReplyChunks` with the same scenario:

- on `main`: `one`..`five` are re-pushed (duplicates);
- with this change: only the chunk after the failure is pushed, `one`..`five` are never re-pushed, and the thrown error carries `{ sentBeforeError: true, visibleReplySent: true }`.

### Real LINE run (live account + API)

Captured a real reply token from an inbound webhook, then drove the real `sendLineReplyChunks` with the real LINE reply/push API. Five short chunks (`c1`..`c5`) fill the reply batch; chunk 6 is 5001 characters, so its push is rejected by LINE with a genuine **HTTP 400** (recipient/token redacted):

**Before (current `main`)** — the reply delivers `c1`..`c5`, the oversized push 400s, and the fallback re-pushes every chunk, so `c1`..`c5` are delivered **twice**:

```
[reply] delivered 5 messages via reply token
[push]  delivered 1 message  (×5  → c1..c5 re-sent)
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? YES (bug)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: false / visibleReplySent: false
```

**After (this change)** — the reply delivers `c1`..`c5`, the oversized push 400s, and the delivered chunks are **not** re-sent; the error is tagged:

```
[reply] delivered 5 messages via reply token
pushed (successful) chunks: []
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? NO (fixed)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: true / visibleReplySent: true
```

In the LINE chat, `c1`..`c5` appear twice before the fix and exactly once after.

### Checks

```
oxfmt --check              → clean (4 files)
oxlint                     → 0 problems
tsgo (extensions)          → no errors in the touched files
check:import-cycles        → 0 runtime value cycles
check:madge-import-cycles  → 0 cycles (reply-chunks ↔ auto-reply-delivery cycle removed)
LINE suite                 → reply-chunks.test.ts + auto-reply-delivery.test.ts: 14 passed
```

target.title: fix(ui): preserve sidebar collapsed state when group rename/delete fails
target.body:
Closes #105974

## What Problem This Solves

Rejected custom-group rename and delete requests left the Gateway catalog unchanged but still rewrote the sidebar's persisted collapsed-group keys. A failed rename could therefore expand the surviving group after reload, while a failed delete could discard its preference entirely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Collapsed-state cleanup ran from `Promise.finally`, so it executed after both successful and rejected RPCs. The sidebar now updates persisted keys only after an explicit completed outcome from the initiating Gateway connection generation. Rejections and completions retired by disconnect/reconnect preserve the existing key byte-for-byte, while the session capability retains current-connection errors for presentation surfaces.

This keeps one authoritative boundary: the Gateway confirms catalog mutations; the sidebar mirrors confirmed results. No new config, migration, protocol, dependency, or compatibility shim.

## User Impact

- Failed rename/delete: the original group and collapsed preference remain intact across reload.
- Successful rename: the collapsed key follows the new group name.
- Successful delete: the obsolete collapsed key is removed.
- A completion from a disconnected, reconnected, or replaced Gateway cannot mutate the new page's browser state.

Sidebar-wide visible mutation feedback remains tracked by #105973; this PR preserves the capability error required by that surface without claiming the dedicated Sessions page automatically displays actions initiated elsewhere.

## Evidence

### Real Gateway reproduction before the fix

Playwright drove the actual Control UI connected to Gateway `2026.7.2` with a real OpenAI-backed disposable session:

1. Created a disposable session and custom group, moved the session into it, and collapsed the group.
2. Renamed the group to a 513-character label so the real Gateway rejected the protocol-invalid request.
3. Observed the server group still present, the original collapsed key missing, the rejected-name key persisted, no danger callout, and one unhandled browser page error.
4. Deleted all disposable session/group/browser state afterward.

### After-fix proof

- Head: `2453ef9fc1a03cd77fb1ad777dd3218abed01471`
- Exact-head real-Gateway proof: Playwright served the CI-built `dist-runtime-build` artifact from run `29250560948` and connected it to the isolated live Gateway `2026.7.2`:
  - Rename rejection: a 513-character target produced a real `INVALID_REQUEST`; the original group stayed visible, its collapsed key stayed present before and after reload, no replacement group appeared, and the browser reported zero page errors.
  - Delete rejection: a temporary SQLite write lock on this disposable Gateway state produced a real `UNAVAILABLE`; the original group and collapsed key stayed present before and after reload with zero page errors. The transaction was rolled back and the lock released immediately after the response.
  - Stale completion: the real Gateway committed a valid rename while Playwright held its response; the application installed a replacement Gateway client before the old response was released. The server contained the renamed group, but the replacement page and a reload retained the original collapsed key and did not add the renamed key. Two WebSocket generations were observed and the browser reported zero page errors.
  - Cleanup: all disposable proof groups were deleted; a direct SQLite count confirmed zero matching rows.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox on behavior-equivalent head `d0e736169c4406d74d96397664302687bd3407ae` (public network, no Tailscale, no IAM role, no credentials; lease `cbx_12a019d28349` released after proof):
  - [run `run_a68b6eef01a5`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_a68b6eef01a5): 76/76 targeted capability and AppSidebar unit tests passed. Browser setup then stopped before E2E because the isolated temporary home lacked Chromium system libraries.
  - [run `run_db8c8595a506`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_db8c8595a506): targeted Chromium Control UI E2E passed 1/1 after installing the required public browser libraries. The rejected rename preserved `category:Research` through reload with no replacement group or page error.
